A separate bucket would change `EXPIRY_HORIZONS`, which is a Largo contract, and the deeper question (why week-old expired prints are in a current-tape panel at all) is a product call. Raised for the coordinator. |
| **Blast radius** | One consumer: the member panel. Largo's copy was already correct. `daysToExpiry` is untouched — its `Math.max(0, …)` clamp is right for its own callers and only masked this on a fallback path that never runs in practice. |
| **Regression guard** | `ExpiryConcentration.test.ts`, +3 tests: expired DTEs (−1, −3, −30, −365) asserted NOT to land in any future horizon; every non-negative boundary pinned (0/1/7/8/30/31/846); and — the anti-drift one — **every DTE from −400 to +900 asserted to bucket identically under `bucketLabel` and Largo's `expiryHorizonLabel`**, so the two cannot silently diverge again. |
| **Status** | FIXED — **pending live validation.** The panel must be observed on production with the 0DTE bucket carrying the expired rows before this is closed. |

## 2026-08-23 — [FINDING, P2 Night Hawk] The 0DTE board told members it was "scanning the whole market" while the market was CLOSED — and contradicted itself on screen doing it — FIXED

> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Symptom** | On a closed market, `/nighthawk` rendered the header badge **`ENGINE Standby ✓`** and, in the same component driven by the same prop, the body text **"Scanning the whole market — no 0DTE setup has cleared the floor right now."** Two contradictory claims visible at once. The second asserts a whole-market sweep RAN and nothing qualified — a statement about a scan that never happened. A member cannot tell "closed" from "open and genuinely nothing qualified", which is the difference between the product resting and the product finding nothing. |
| **Root cause** | `containers.tsx` computed `emptyHint` as a **binary** — `degraded ? outage : "Scanning the whole market…"` — but the deck has **three** states: degraded · not-scanning (CLOSED/PRE_MARKET) · scanning-and-empty. The third state silently borrowed the wording of the second. Compounding it, the local `BoardRespWithSession` type modelled `session.heat` as `{ state }` only, **dropping `note`** — the data layer's own member-facing sentence has always been on the wire, but the deck could not reach it. The authors had already fixed the *first* instance of exactly this bug (the comment at `containers.tsx:86` explains why a degraded board must not be painted as a calm flat tape) and stopped one state short. |
| **Evidence** | Live render of production, Sat 2026-08-23 00:40 UTC, via `proxy-browser.cjs` at 1440×900 and 430×932 — **114 / 101 requests routed, 0 fail**, marks SSE held open, so a clean render rather than a harness artifact. Reproduced identically at both viewports. The board payload at that instant was **entirely honest**: `session.trading_day:false`, `session.heat:{state:"CLOSED", note:"No session today — Night Hawk's evening playbook covers the next open."}`, and BOTH discovery lanes `{"status":"off_hours"}`. Nothing was missing; the UI had every fact and discarded them. |
| **Fix** | New pure `src/features/nighthawk/lib/deck-empty-hint.ts` → `zeroDteEmptyHint({degraded, heatState, heatNote})`, three-way. It **prefers the payload's own `heat.note`** over new invented copy so `board.ts sessionHeat` stays the single source of truth for this wording; the in-module literals are only a fallback for a legacy payload without `note`. `BoardRespWithSession` widened to carry `note`. |
| **Blast radius** | **One call site — the 0DTE deck.** The other two `emptyHint` sites were examined and deliberately left alone: `HorizonDeck` (Swings/LEAPS) makes a different claim ("this lane is coming online") on a phase cadence, not an RTH sweep; `LegacyDeck` is the evening edition with no session heat and already-accurate copy ("Five ranked setups land here after the evening scan · ~5:30 PM ET"). An earlier note in PR #2659 called this a three-site defect — that was **wrong and is corrected here**. `POST_COMMIT`/`LATE_SESSION` also deliberately keep the scanning sentence: G-14 blocks new *directional* commits after 15:30 ET but credit/condor seats stay eligible, so the board really is still scanning. |
| **Fix rationale** | Narrowed a false claim rather than inventing a new "unknown" state: an unknown/null heat state falls through to the prior scanning wording, because the deck has no design for a third visual state and adding one would be scope the evidence does not support. Reused `heat.note` rather than writing parallel copy, since two sentences describing one state is how they drift apart. |
| **Regression guard** | `src/features/nighthawk/lib/deck-empty-hint.test.ts`, 9 tests — the shipped defect reproduced from the REAL observed payload; `heat.note` preferred; PRE_MARKET (wrong every weekday before 09:30, not just weekends); legacy/blank-note fallback never falling through to the scan claim; **RTH/OPENING_DRIVE unchanged**; POST_COMMIT/LATE_SESSION pinned as deliberate; degraded still winning over closed; unknown state falling through; case-insensitivity. Suites: nighthawk lib **768 pass / 0 fail** (was 759), command-deck **324 pass / 0 fail**, `tsc --noEmit` clean, Node 20.20.2. |
| **Status** | FIXED — **pending live validation.** Merged is not done: re-render `/nighthawk` on production after deploy and confirm the closed-market sentence replaces the scan claim. This one is cheaply verifiable off-hours, unlike NH-2. |

## 2026-08-23 — [FINDING, P2 Largo] Three hand-written `coverage: 1` literals survived #2626 — one of them leaves the process — FIXED

> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Symptom** | `coverage` is `verified / total`; at `total === 0` that is `0/0`, and `1` advertises a data-less answer as **perfectly grounded**. #2626 fixed that at the source in `verifyClaims`, but three hand-written copies of the forbidden shape survived it in `largo-terminal.ts`'s error paths — `{ total: 0, verified: 0, coverage: 1, unverified: [] }` at `:1149`, `:1167` and `:1454`. The one at `:1167` is the **returned payload** of the non-streaming API's internal-error response, so the fabricated value leaves the process. |
| **Root cause** | The fix was applied to the producer and not to the shape. `ClaimVerification.coverage` is legitimately `number \| null`, so every literal compiled and nothing could object. This is the same defect class as the fabricated `confidence` the product contract forbids: a score a product cannot calibrate must be OMITTED, never invented, because it is compared against another lane's MEASURED one. |
| **Evidence** | Traced per-site during the Phase 0 map (`LARGO-ENGINE-MAP.md` §4): `:1149` and `:1454` feed `logClaudeTurn`, which nulls `claims_total`/`claims_verified` on the error path, so they are inert today; **`:1167` escapes**, on `runLargoQuery`'s catch. Severity is bounded because the browser always streams and Largo is launch-gated, so the reachable population is the non-streaming API and admin/grant viewers. |
| **Fix** | One constructor, `unverifiedTurn()`, exported from `verifier.ts` beside the type it builds, returning `coverage: null`. All three literals replaced. A convention ("remember to use null") gets skipped; a constructor cannot be. Same reasoning as the stop-reason union that was deduplicated rather than re-guarded — remove the second copy instead of policing it. |
| **Blast radius** | Both `runLargoQuery` and `runLargoQueryStream` error paths. No client consumer reads the returned `verification` field (checked), and `applyVerificationCaveat`/`auditLargoAnswerGrounding` already guard `coverage != null`, so nothing coerces the null into a 0 and reports a data-less turn as 0% grounded. |
| **Fix rationale** | Deliberately NOT widened into a general "no fabricated numbers" sweep — the contract's `confidence` rule was swept separately (`LARGO-ENGINE-MAP.md` §4b, clean in this layer, two candidates routed to other lanes). This is the one surviving instance of the `coverage` shape. |
| **Regression guard** | `src/lib/largo/no-fabricated-coverage.test.ts` (6 tests): the constructor returns null; **no `coverage: 1` literal survives anywhere in the turn pipeline** (source assertion, comments stripped first so the explanation cannot satisfy the assertion it explains); exactly three constructed call sites, so a fourth error path cannot hand-roll one; the caveat does not fire on a claimless turn; the constructed shape agrees with what `verifyClaims` itself returns on a claimless answer, so the two cannot drift into disagreeing about the same situation; and the cron does not flag a claimless turn. **Proven to fire**: restoring one literal fails 2 of the 6; restoring the constructor passes 6/6. |
| **Status** | FIXED — verified by construction. The value is inert on two of the three sites and the third is only reachable through the non-streaming API, so there is no member-visible behaviour change to observe on production; the guard is what carries this forward. |

## 2026-08-23 — [FINDING, P2 Largo] `/terminal` displayed a hardcoded "AI Online" badge — lit green through a total outage, on a claim nothing measured — FIXED

> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Symptom** | The Largo page header rendered `AI Online` with a green status dot. It was a **hardcoded literal** — no prop, no state, no health read — so it could not be false. It rendered green during a complete Largo outage, and would render green with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` removed entirely. |
| **Root cause** | `src/features/largo/components/LargoPageShell.tsx` passed `badge={<Badge tone="accent" dot>AI Online</Badge>}` as a static JSX literal. Nothing in the component reads any liveness signal. |
| **Evidence** | Rendered on PRODUCTION at both viewports via `proxy-browser.cjs` (`Routed: 108 ok, 0 fail` desktop 1440x900; `102 ok, 0 fail` mobile 430x932): **"AI ONLINE", green, on both** — while every Largo turn was failing at round 0 with HTTP 400 *"Your credit balance is too low to access the Anthropic API"* (confirmed from the production log). Found by LOOKING at the rendered page under the corrected `_COMMON` rule 6b, not by reading code. |
| **The irony that makes it a finding, not a nit** | The status endpoint rendered *directly below* this header states the exact principle in its own docstring: *"a row of dots that are green because they are hard-coded green says the opposite the first time a member sees one lit during an outage"* (`app/api/market/largo/status/route.ts`). It honours that for all six PRODUCT dots, each derived from that system's own production reader. The AI's own dot was the single exception, one component higher — and it was lit during precisely the outage that sentence describes. |
| **Fix** | The badge is **omitted**, not replaced. Per the product contract's rule for exactly this case: a value that cannot be calibrated is OMITTED, never fabricated. Nothing today measures whether the model can answer — `/status` deliberately makes **no Anthropic call** ("NO ANTHROPIC CALL, no tool loop, no cost"), and inferring liveness from the API key being present is what produced the defect. The reasoning is left in place as a comment so the next person does not re-add it because the header looks unfinished. |
| **Blast radius** | `/terminal` at every viewport, for every viewer (admins and `tool_access` grantees today, since Largo is launch-gated). The live status strip below — LIVE/CLOSED, data age, N/6 systems online — is derived from real reads and is untouched; this removes the false claim, not the true one. |
| **Fix rationale** | A real signal becomes available once the tool loop reports `upstream_error` (`ToolLoopStopReason`, PR #2653): a badge could then read recent turns' stop reasons and be *true*. **Deliberately not wired here** — that would be an ordering dependency on an unmerged PR, and `CLAUDE.md` carries the incident that pattern caused. Honest omission now; a measured badge when there is something to measure. |
| **Regression guard** | `src/features/largo/components/largo-shell-no-fabricated-status.test.ts` (4 tests): no hardcoded `AI Online`; no hardcoded liveness word passed as a `badge`; the explanatory comment survives (naming both the live symptom and the contract rule); and the terminal still mounts, so the real status strip was not removed with the false one. Comments are stripped before matching so the explanation cannot satisfy the assertion it explains. A badge driven by a prop/state/fetch is explicitly permitted — the guard forbids only the unmeasured literal. **Proven to fire**: re-adding the badge fails 2 of the 4 tests; restoring passes 4/4. |
| **Status** | FIXED — verified by construction (the claim is gone from the source and the guard fires). A post-deploy render should confirm the header no longer asserts liveness. |

## 2026-08-23 — [FINDING, P1 Largo] Every tool result's size was measured and never compared to the transport cap, so no truncation was detectable — FIXED (detection)

> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Symptom** | An over-cap tool result still "succeeds": `anthropicToolLoop` keeps the first 16,000 characters, appends `…[truncated]`, the call returns, the loop completes, and the model writes a fluent answer from the fragment. Nothing in the codebase objected. Three defects shipped exactly that way — #2433 (`get_zerodte_record` delivering **1.5%** of itself with every aggregate gone), #2436 (`get_nighthawk_edition` cutting off every play), #2480 (`get_nighthawk_outcomes` quoting a **40% win rate over "5 plays"** for a window whose real record was **74 resolved at 50%**) — and each was found only by asking the LIVE model whether its payload had arrived. |
| **Root cause** | `makeGuardedToolRunner` (`src/lib/largo/core/tool-guard.ts`) has recorded `bytes: sizeOf(result)` on **every** tool call since it shipped, and nothing ever compared that number to `MAX_TOOL_RESULT_CHARS`. `formatToolDiagnostics` flagged `DENIED`, `FAILED` and `EMPTY` (bytes === 0) — but not over-cap. The measurement was already in hand; only the comparison was missing. It could not easily be added, either: the constant lived in `providers/anthropic.ts`, which at module scope imports the Anthropic SDK, API telemetry, the Redis cache client and a Discord notifier, and constructs a `SpendTracker` — while `tool-guard.ts` is deliberately kept free of that graph ("injected so this module stays free of the 116-tool dependency graph"). The one file that could detect truncation could not see the number defining it. |
| **Evidence** | Phase 0 inventory (`docs/bie/LARGO-ENGINE-MAP.md` §3): of **129** tools, exactly **2** (`get_zerodte_record`, `get_nighthawk_outcomes`) bound their payload with `fitRowsToBudget` before the transport's blind cut — and those are precisely the two someone had already caught truncating. **A third was found by hand within hours of that inventory**: #2649 fitted `get_vector_full_state`, which was shipping Vector's entire bead rail (~4,077 chars for ONE oracle bead) into the same 16k cap. That is the argument for this change in one line — the count of *known* over-cap tools moves only when a human happens to look, because nothing measures it. The remaining ~126 are still capped with nothing watching. The serialized tool block itself is 99,540 chars. |
| **Fix** | `MAX_TOOL_RESULT_CHARS` extracted to `src/lib/providers/tool-result-cap.ts`, a dependency-free module, alongside `exceedsToolResultCap(bytes)`; `providers/anthropic.ts` re-exports it so every existing import is unchanged. `ToolCallDiagnostic` gains `truncated: boolean`, derived from the size the guard already measured. `formatToolDiagnostics` renders `TRUNCATED <bytes>/<cap>` per tool and counts them in the summary line. The size is included because it is the actionable part: *"get_zerodte_record 1200ms TRUNCATED 41203/16000"* says how much must come off and whether the fix is pagination or a leaner shape. |
| **Blast radius** | Every one of the 129 tools, on every Largo turn, both depths, both the streaming and non-streaming paths — the guard is the single tool-execution path. Detection only: **no tool's payload changes**, and the transport's behaviour is untouched. |
| **Fix rationale** | Detection was chosen over raising the cap or auto-paginating. Raising the cap trades one silent overflow for a slower, more expensive one and still has no observer; auto-pagination changes what 129 tools return, which is a per-tool judgment (aggregates first, sample last) that `fit-tool-result.ts` already encodes and cannot be applied blind. Deliberately unchanged: `bytes === 0` still reads `EMPTY` rather than "unknown", a pre-existing conflation for non-serializable results that is a separate, smaller issue. `exceedsToolResultCap` rejects non-finite input so an unmeasurable result is never reported as huge. |
| **Regression guard** | `src/lib/largo/core/tool-guard.test.ts` +8: over-cap flagged with its size; under-cap not flagged; **boundary at exactly the cap is NOT truncated** (the loop cuts on strictly greater-than, and an off-by-one would cry wolf on the tools closest to the limit — the ones whose reports most need to be believed); zero/NaN/Infinity never truncated; TRUNCATED coexists with DENIED/FAILED/EMPTY without masking them; end-to-end through the real runner with an over-cap fixture and with a small one; and — the load-bearing one — **the guard's `bytes` is asserted equal to `JSON.stringify(returned).length`, the exact string the transport measures**, so the flag is a fact about the transport rather than an estimate of one. That equivalence is invisible from either file alone. |
| **Status** | FIXED (detection) — **pending live validation.** The log line cannot be observed on production until the upstream Anthropic credit outage clears and Largo completes turns again. What it will then answer for the first time: which of the 129 tools are actually over the cap. That measurement is also the prerequisite for re-arming `largo-truncation-probe.mjs`, whose control (`get_nighthawk_outcomes@window_days=180`) was fixed by #2480/#2628 and so now returns COMPLETE, correctly marking every run UNVERIFIED until a new over-cap control is chosen — from measured sizes rather than guesswork. |

## 2026-08-22 — [FINDING, P1 Largo] Eight tool-loop outcomes collapsed into one bare `null`, so a billing failure was narrated to members as "I couldn't pull enough live data" — FIXED

> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Symptom** | For a full day, **every** Largo question returned *"I couldn't pull enough live data to answer that — try naming a ticker or asking about SPX structure."* The desk's data was fine. The real cause was an HTTP 400 from Anthropic — *"Your credit balance is too low to access the Anthropic API"* — confirmed from the production log. Members (and three separate agent lanes) were told the platform had no data for what was an account-level billing failure, and the advice offered ("name a ticker") could not possibly help, because it addressed a cause that was not the cause. |
| **Root cause** | `anthropicToolLoop` (`src/lib/providers/anthropic.ts`) returns `string \| null`, and **eight structurally different outcomes** all returned that same bare `null`: AI gate closed, no API key, spend ceiling pre-flight, wall-clock budget exhausted, spend ceiling mid-loop, a model create/stream that threw after retries **including the escalation retry**, an empty model round, and rounds exhausted with a failed synthesis pass. `classifyEmptyAnswer` therefore had nothing to classify *from*, guessed off elapsed time, and defaulted to `no_data`. Only ONE of the eight is actually a data gap. |
| **Evidence** | Nine live production turns (admin session — Largo is launch-gated: `LAUNCHED_TOOLS = heatmap,nighthawk`, `defaultLaunched:false`), both depths, all returning the `no_data` copy: concrete 3546 ms, deep 3711 ms, concrete **924 ms**, deep 4067 ms, plus five truncation-probe turns. `tools_used` was `[live_feed_capture, platform_vitals_prefetch]` every time — the seed plus one prefetch marker, i.e. **zero model dispatches**. Sub-second latency against the 20–45 s a real Deep turn takes proves the loop returned at or before round 0. Because #2582 retries round 0 on `LARGO_ESCALATION_MODEL`, a failing turn attempts **three distinct models across the two depths** (sonnet-5 → sonnet-4-6, haiku-4-5 → sonnet-4-6), and `shouldFallBackToEscalationModel`'s own docstring names that signature: *"on a non-transient fault (a 400, an auth/spend error) both models fail."* Confirmed from the production log (coordinator, AWS access): `[anthropic] 400 {"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"Your credit balance is too low to access the Anthropic API…"}` followed by `[anthropic] tool-loop round create failed — falling back to accumulated assistant text` and `[anthropic] round 0 create on claude-haiku-4-5 failed — retrying once on claude-sonnet-4-6`, across dozens of requests, both models, every depth. That confirms the **throw** sub-case, not the empty-round one — so `upstream_error` is the reason this turn now reports. |
| **Fix** | The loop now reports which exit it took. New `ToolLoopStopReason` union (`answered`/`ai_disabled`/`not_configured`/`spend_ceiling`/`upstream_error`/`empty_round`/`loop_budget`/`max_rounds`) delivered through an optional `onStop` callback, fired exactly once by a `stop()` wrapper that all nine `return`s now go through. `classifyEmptyAnswer` gains three causes (`provider_error`, `unavailable`, `empty_round`) and — the load-bearing rule — **a reported reason outranks the elapsed-time heuristic**: a fact must never lose to a guess. Both Largo call sites capture and pass it. |
| **Blast radius** | Both `runLargoQuery` and `runLargoQueryStream` — the browser always takes the streaming path, so that was the one members actually saw. Reported via callback rather than by widening the return type, so every existing caller compiles and behaves identically; the only two callers are Largo's own. The provider's error text is passed as `detail` **to the log only** — it can name our billing state, so no member is ever shown it (a regression test asserts the copy contains no `credit`/`balance`/`400`/`anthropic`). Also corrected the empty-round `console.warn`, which promised the *old* member copy: a log line naming the wrong member-facing message sends whoever greps it to the wrong branch. |
| **Fix rationale** | Fixing this would **not** have prevented the outage — the billing failure is real and upstream. It would have made the outage self-describing instead of costing three lanes a day of investigation, and stopped the engine blaming its own data for an account problem. Deliberately unchanged: `answered` and `max_rounds` still fall through to the existing heuristics, because neither carries more information than elapsed time does. The copy names *no* provider detail and no machinery nouns (no "model", "tool", "prefetch", "API"), per the same discipline `never-narrate-machinery.test.ts` enforces on the system prompt. |
| **Regression guard** | `src/lib/largo/empty-answer-fallback.test.ts`, +7 tests: an upstream failure is never narrated as missing data; the provider message never reaches the member; **a stated reason beats the elapsed-time guess in both directions**; every stop reason maps to its own cause; only a genuine data gap may emit the "no data" string; an empty round says the data was not the problem and uses no internal vocabulary; full back-compat with no reason supplied. `anthropic-stream-guard.test.ts` and `anthropic-empty-round-visibility.test.ts` updated to the new return shape — the degradation behaviour they guard is unchanged, the reason now rides alongside it. |
| **Secondary finding** | The first draft duplicated the stop-reason union into `empty-answer-fallback.ts` and pinned the copies with a type-level assertion **in the test file**. That guard was **inert** — `tsconfig.json` excludes `**/*.test.ts`, so `tsc` never checks it; proven by deliberately drifting one union and watching the build stay green. The duplicate was deleted rather than re-guarded (the loop owns the type, the pure module imports it type-only, so drift is now impossible by construction). **General note for the repo: a compile-time assertion written in a `*.test.ts` file does nothing here.** |
| **Status** | FIXED — **pending live validation.** Merged is not done: the outage is upstream and still open at time of writing, so the new copy cannot yet be observed on production. Once Largo answers again, an induced failure (or the next real one) must be seen rendering `provider_error` rather than the data-gap copy. |

## 2026-08-23 — [FINDING, P1 Thermal/Largo] `walls_by_horizon` was assigned in one place that never fires on a fresh build — the DTE-scoped walls shipped ABSENT on every ticker — FIXED

> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Symptom** | `gex.walls_by_horizon` — the 0DTE / 3DTE / 7DTE wall breakdown — was `undefined` on every served matrix, so `get_gex_heatmap.walls_by_horizon` was `null` in practice and the Thermal payload offered no way to name which expiry scope a wall belongs to. |
| **Root cause** | `src/lib/providers/polygon-options-gex.ts:1460` was the **only** assignment, inside `prunePastExpiriesFromHeatmap`. That function early-returns the heatmap **unchanged** when `heatmapHasPastExpiries` is false (`polygon-options-gex.ts:1356`) — and fresh builds already filter `expiry < today` at ingest inside `accumulateContract`, so the prune is always a no-op on a fresh matrix. The literal that actually ships, `buildGexHeatmapUncached`'s `gex: {…}` object, omitted the field entirely. Net effect: the horizons appeared only on a cached matrix that happened to survive an ET date rollover. |
| **Evidence** | Live production read 2026-08-22 23:21Z through one temp Clerk admin/premium user, six tickers: **SPY, SPX, QQQ, NVDA, MSFT, AAPL — `walls_by_horizon` ABSENT on all six**, including two matrices already 1.7 h old (MSFT `asof` age 6,040 s, AAPL 6,252 s), which rules out "not warmed yet". |
| **Why P1** | The served `call_wall` is a **fifteen-expiry aggregate** running ~three weeks out. Measured on SPX 2026-08-20 at spot 7641.16 the aggregate read **7800 (+2.1%)** while the front expiry alone read **7700 (+0.8%)**. A wall 2.1% OTM is not actionable on a 0DTE trade, and reading the aggregate as near-dated is the natural mistake. `walls_by_horizon` exists precisely to make that difference visible — it was the fix for that ambiguity, and it was not shipping. Same "right number, missing scope" family as 0DTE max pain quoting a settled session. |
| **Fix** | Two assignments, because one alone would have created the next defect. (1) `buildGexHeatmapUncached` now publishes `walls_by_horizon: wallsByHorizon(gexBuilt.cells, today, spot)`. (2) `recomputeNearTermGexStrikeTotals` (`spx-odte-gex-uw-overlay.ts`) recomputes it too, and `applySpxOdteGexUwOverlayWithLadder` passes its pinned session date through. Without (2), populating (1) would have left the SPX overlay carrying a **pre-overlay 0DTE wall** beside a post-overlay flip, wall pair and regime — the overlay REPLACES today's 0DTE column, so 0DTE is the one bucket it definitionally invalidates. |
| **Fix rationale** | `wallsByHorizon` is pure and cheap (a re-sum of cells already in hand, no fetch) and filters to DTE ≤ 7 itself, so passing the full near+far axis is correct — far-dated monthly columns fall outside every bucket by construction. It also already side-constrains each bucket via `wallsFromStrikeTotals(totals, spot)`, so the horizons inherit #2417's no-wrong-side-wall rule for free. The aggregate `call_wall`/`put_wall` are **deliberately unchanged**: what "near-term" should mean is a product decision, and the fix is to publish the horizons beside the aggregate, not to redefine it. |
| **Deliberately NOT fixed** | `buildGexHeatmapFromUwStrikeExposures` (the degraded UW fallback when the Polygon chain is empty/403) still omits the field, now with a comment and a test saying why. UW `/spot-exposures/strike` returns an **all-expiry** ladder with no per-row expiry, and the fallback files every strike under a single synthetic `{ [today]: net }` column — bucketing that would return the same whole-chain wall in all three buckets and label the first "0DTE", asserting a DTE breakdown the source cannot support. An omitted optional field says "not computable here"; three identical buckets would be a fabricated one. |
| **Blast radius** | `polygon-options-gex.ts` is SHARED with Vector — checked: the only consumer of `walls_by_horizon` anywhere in the repo is `src/lib/largo/gex-heatmap-for-largo.ts:190`, which already maps it and already handles absence (`?? null`). The change is purely additive to an optional field that was previously always absent, so no Vector-side behaviour changes; no Vector file reads it. Cached payloads written before this deploy simply keep the old `undefined` until their next rebuild (≤ the 5 s matrix TTL in practice), which the field's optional/additive contract already covers. |
| **Regression guard** | `spx-odte-gex-uw-overlay.test.ts` — three behavioural tests: the overlay recomputes the block from the OVERLAID column (stale strikes seeded as 9999/1000, values the book cannot produce, so recompute and inherit are distinguishable); the buckets stay side-constrained where a strike **more negative but above spot** must not become the put wall; and a pinned session date drives the DTE buckets. `gex-regime-invariant.test.ts` — three source invariants: the fresh build publishes the field, the prune path still does, the overlay recomputes it alongside the flip, and the UW fallback still does not. 618 pass / 0 fail across providers + gex + thermal + heatmap-route on Node 20; `tsc --noEmit` clean. |
| **Two wrong assertions caught while writing the tests** | Recorded because both are the map's own documented traps, hit live. First draft asserted the recomputed 0DTE call wall `!== 7800` — but 7800 **is** the correct post-overlay value, so the assertion proved nothing in either direction. Second draft asserted a put wall at a strike carrying **+835 m**: a wall is defined by the SIGN of net dealer gamma, not by which side of spot it sits on, so an all-positive fixture has no put wall at all. The code was right both times. |
| **Status** | FIXED. |

## 2026-08-22 — [FINDING, P2 Meridian] `reaction_basis` / `reaction_settled` reached the UI and NO component read them — assumptions and still-moving numbers rendered as settled measurements — FIXED

> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Symptom** | Every earnings reaction on the Meridian desk rendered as a bare percentage — `· −4.2% reaction` — whether it was a settled measurement, a number **still moving** because the session had not closed, or a number measured on an **assumed** session because the print's timing was never resolved. A member had no way to tell the three apart. |
| **Root cause** | `meridian-reaction-core.ts` computes `reaction_basis`, `reaction_measure` and `reaction_settled` for exactly this purpose, and `meridian-types.ts:406` instructs in so many words: *"Mark these in the UI."* They are computed, typed, tested, and carried all the way to the component props — and a grep of `src/features/meridian/**` found all three **only in the type definition**. Three render sites (`MeridianEarningsTabs.tsx:485`, `MeridianEarningsIntelPanel.tsx:110`, `MeridianEarningsHistoryPanel.tsx:37`) each printed `row.reaction_pct ?? row.session_change_pct` and nothing else. A correct payload with a lossy consumer — the shape `_COMMON.md` §6b names. |
| **Evidence — the assumed half** | Live 2026-08-22, 11,956 settled Benzinga prints (2026-02-01 → 2026-08-21): 219 (**1.8%**; 0.5% at `importance>=3`) carry a mid-session timestamp and therefore `assumed_report_session`. **All 219 have a time field — none are null**, so this is not a coverage gap, it is genuine ambiguity. Over the 25 such `importance>=3` prints, reading them as AMC instead moves the value by a median 2.82pp (max 15.24) and **flips the sign on 12 of 25 = 48%**. e.g. `ASMIY 2026-03-03` displays **+11.60%**; as AMC it is **−3.64%**. |
| **Evidence — the unsettled half, which is larger** | `reaction_settled` exists because production served a moving number as a measurement: 2026-08-21 at 09:46 ET, on a session closing at 16:00, `BEKE` came back −4.74 and then −4.24 **between two reads a minute apart** — the number disproving its own label while you watch. This is not a 1.8% slice. During RTH it is **every print reporting that morning**. |
| **Fix** | One pure helper, `src/features/meridian/lib/meridian-reaction-display.ts`, stating the rule once: `reactionQualifier()` returns a mark + a full-sentence tooltip for an unsettled (`live`) or assumed (`assumed`) reaction and **null for the common settled case**, so the UI stays quiet rather than badging every row. Rendered by one shared `<ReactionFlag>` in `meridian-ui.tsx` at both list sites. Unsettled outranks assumed when both apply — "still moving" is the more urgent fact. |
| **Fix — the part that is not cosmetic** | `MeridianEarningsHistoryPanel` fed **all** prints into implied-vs-realized. A still-forming reaction is not a realized outcome and an assumed one may be measuring the wrong session, so pooling either into "what this company usually does on earnings" launders an unknown into a statistic — precisely the `_COMMON.md` §7 failure. `settledReactions()` now filters the distribution and the panel **states the held-out count** rather than the list quietly getting shorter. |
| **Fix rationale** | A tooltip carries the consequence, not just the caveat: the assumed one says the number *can carry the opposite sign*, because "timing unknown" alone does not tell a reader that 48% of these invert. The badge is deliberately low-contrast and small — it qualifies the number, it must not compete with it. |
| **Blast radius** | All three sites that render a reaction, plus the pooled distribution. The Largo boundary was **not** affected and is unchanged: `print_history` already carried all three fields to the model, so this was UI-only. Verified by grep that no fourth render site exists; the shared component means a future one inherits the marking rather than re-omitting it. |
| **Regression guard** | `src/features/meridian/lib/meridian-reaction-display.test.ts` — 6 tests: settled needs no qualifier, unsettled marks `live` (the BEKE case), assumed marks `assumed` **and the tooltip names the sign risk**, unsettled outranks assumed, an unmeasured row is not badged, and `settledReactions` pools only what may honestly be pooled. **501 pass / 0 fail** across all 40 Meridian test files on Node 20.20.2; tsc clean; `client-server-boundary` 4/4 (the helper is type-only, safe inside a `"use client"` tree). |
| **Status** | FIXED. |

## 2026-08-23 — [FINDING, P2 Vector/tooling] `vector-ui-walkthrough.cjs` reported 15 FAILs against a `/vector` desk that renders perfectly — stale selectors, a nav race, and a panel that no component mounts — FIXED

> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Symptom** | First live interaction run of the Vector lane: **15 of 16 states FAIL**, `routing failures: 0`. Reported "GEX ladder has no rows", "side panel missing: ladder", "side panel missing: pulse", "no effect: the click had no effect", "daily chart container missing", "select is `undefined`". A screenshot of the same run shows the desk **rendering correctly** — matrix rail populated with strikes 205–228, chart drawn, play card, technicals, alerts, live Helix tape. |
| **Root cause** | Three independent staleness defects plus a race. **(1)** The rail is `VectorOdteMatrixRail` with classes `vector-odte-matrix-*`; the harness still queried `.vector-gex-ladder`, `.vector-gex-ladder-rows`, `.vector-gex-ladder-spot`, `.vector-gex-ladder-sub` — all absent. A `vector-gex-ladder-reset` **class** still exists on the rail, which is the fossil that makes the mistake look right. **(2)** The chart-view control is a **button group** (`role="group"` of `<button data-testid="vector-chart-view-{1d,1w,4h,intraday}">`), and the harness drove it with `selectOption` on the group — hence `select is "undefined"`. **(3)** `.vector-pulse` is rendered by `VectorPulse.tsx`, which **is imported by no component and not exported from the feature index** — it cannot render on any shell, so that assertion could never pass. **(4)** `captureApiBaseline` ran `page.evaluate` straight after `domcontentloaded`; `/vector` is client-hydrated and `VectorPageClient` calls `router.replace`, destroying the execution context mid-evaluate. That killed the entire run before a single state was asserted on **2 of 3 attempts** — a race, so it passed when written and looked fine. |
| **Evidence** | Live DOM probe through the CONNECT tunnel (96 requests routed, 0 fail) enumerating all 27 `data-testid`s and every ladder/matrix class actually on the page. Every `vector-gex-ladder-*` selector: **MISSING**. `vector-chart-view-select` present but as a group, with four per-view button testids beside it. After the fix, the same harness on the same page: **16/16 ok, 0 failing, 0 skipped, 175 requests routed, 0 fail.** |
| **Why it matters more than P2 suggests** | A harness that cries wolf on a healthy product is worse than no harness: it trains the next reader to skim its output. That is the identical argument this repo already made about `cron-schedule-coverage.mjs`'s unexplained bucket, and about the SPX "GEX ladder unavailable" case this file's own header cites. This one had drifted far enough to be pure noise — and it is the ONLY interaction harness on the desk's flagship page. |
| **Fix** | Selectors updated to the live DOM (`vector-odte-matrix-*`, `[data-testid=vector-odte-matrix-reset]`). Chart-view steps changed from `selectOption` to a click on the per-view testid with an `active` effect check (the buttons already set `aria-pressed` / `is-active`). The `.vector-pulse` side-panel assertion replaced with `.vector-technicals-panel` — the card that was **extracted from** VectorPulse's intel grid and IS mounted. `captureApiBaseline` now waits for `[data-testid=vector-page-toolbar]` (which exists only after hydration) and retries **once** on "Execution context was destroyed" — once, because the context is destroyed exactly once by the replace; a second failure is a different cause and should surface. |
| **A verdict-quality fix in the same pass** | The VEX lens step reported "the click had no effect". It is not a defect: `VectorLensToggle.tsx:51` **disables** the VEX button when `vexAvailable` is false, precisely so a member cannot select a lens with no data behind it. The harness now reports a disabled control as **NOT EXERCISED** rather than FAILED — the honest verdict, since the control was there, was deliberately inert, and the interaction it guards remains unverified. Turning correct absence-handling into a defect is the same absence-vs-fault confusion this fleet keeps paying for, arriving from the tooling side. |
| **Blast radius** | One harness. No product code touched — the product was never broken. Two other Vector harnesses reference the rail (`vector-bead-pixel-audit.cjs`, `vector-rail-visibility-shot.cjs`); **not** swept here because they were not run and a blind rename is how the next stale selector gets shipped. Flagged for their own verification run. |
| **Also found, NOT fixed here** | `src/features/vector/components/VectorPulse.tsx` — **528 lines, imported by nothing.** Only reference is `vector-ios-native.test.ts`, which reads its source as *text* to check iOS CSS conventions. Its TECHNICALS card was extracted into `VectorTechnicalsPanel`; whether the rest was retired on purpose or orphaned is a product decision, not a harness fix, so it is raised rather than deleted. (Checked and ruled out: the mobile shell's `pulse` segment is labelled **"Helix"** and renders the tape — it does not mount VectorPulse, so no member-facing surface is empty.) |
| **Regression guard** | The harness is its own guard and is now falsifiable in both directions: it went 15-FAIL → 16-OK on an unchanged product, and the run is repeatable. Desktop 16/16 ok. Mobile (`--mobile`, iOS shell) 0 failing with **10 of 16 controls not rendered on the default segment** — reported honestly as NOT EXERCISED rather than passed, and logged as a real coverage gap: the harness never switches iOS segments, so the mobile interaction layer is still unverified. |
| **Status** | FIXED (the harness). The mobile-segment coverage gap and the orphaned `VectorPulse` are OPEN and recorded. |

## 2026-08-23 — [FINDING, P4 Vector/Largo] `get_vector_analytics` had spent its whole transport safety margin, and the one parameter a model can vary was the one eating it — FIXED

> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Symptom** | No live truncation — and that is the honest headline. `get_vector_analytics` fits the 16,000-char transport cap at every `regimeDays` its own clamp accepts. What it had lost was the MARGIN: at the default it sits exactly on `LARGO_RESULT_CHAR_BUDGET` (14,000), and from `regimeDays ≈ 16` upward it is past it. |
| **Root cause** | The payload is assembled from sections each individually capped (`MAX_SCREENER_ROWS = 15` × 3 presets, `MAX_PIVOTS = 12`, `MAX_EVENTS = 8`, `MAX_BUCKETS = 8`) and then returned with no budget over the WHOLE. Two of those caps are large — `screener` alone is ~49% of the payload — and one section, `daily_regime`, scales linearly with `regimeDays`, which is **caller-settable** and clamped to `[1, 30]` by `clampDailyRegimeDays`. So the single knob a model can turn is the one that consumes the remaining headroom. `LARGO_RESULT_CHAR_BUDGET` sits below the transport cap deliberately, because "a caller may still round, wrap or annotate the object afterwards"; that reserve was gone. |
| **Evidence** | Reconstruction of the payload at the tool's own documented caps with realistic values (a construction, not a live capture): `regimeDays` 1 → 12,622 chars (79% of cap, under budget); **15 (default) → 13,938 (87%, exactly at the 14,000 budget)**; 22 → 14,596 (91%, over budget); 30 → 15,348 (96%, over budget). |
| **A correction this finding carries** | An earlier revision of `VECTOR-MAP.md` §6, #2649's commit message and its PR thread all stated `regimeDays = 30` at **16,358 chars — 102%, over the transport cap.** That was **wrong**: it modelled `ticker_comparison` at fifteen rows, but `buildTickerComparisonRows` is capped by `DEFAULT_MAX_COMPARISONS = 4`, so the strip is the active ticker plus at most four peers — five rows, ~534 chars, not ~1,544. Severity was downgraded P3 → P4 accordingly. Every other cap in that reconstruction was read out of the source; this one was assumed because the screener's fifteen sat beside it in the same payload. **An estimate is only as good as its least-checked input, and the least-checked one is the one that looked like its neighbour.** |
| **Fix** | New `src/lib/largo/vector-analytics-fit.ts` — `fitVectorAnalyticsForModel`, applied in `vectorAnalyticsForLargo` AFTER `roundFloats` (rounding shrinks the payload, so fitting first would budget against wider numbers than are served). A cumulative reduction ladder trims in ascending order of information-per-byte — `daily_regime.rows` first (multi-session history, and the caller-settable growth term), then the three `screener` preset row lists, then `market_structure.pivots` — stopping at the first rung that fits. `market_structure.events` and `latest_event` are **never** sampled: the BOS/CHoCH read is the actionable part. Floors (3 regime rows / 5 screener rows / 6 pivots) stop the ladder before a section becomes uninformative. |
| **Fix rationale** | Trimming, not raising the cap, and not deleting sections. Each preset's `returned` / `truncated` are **recomputed** from what survives so they can never claim rows the payload no longer carries, while `matched_universe` / `rankable_rows` / `excluded_no_metric` pass through untouched — those are facts about the SCREEN, not the sample, and are exactly what the tool description tells the model to quote. The `fit` block is inserted after the time anchors rather than appended, because #2649 established that the transport's cut is a HEAD slice and whatever sits last is what goes first — a disclosure block is the worst thing to lose. |
| **Blast radius** | One tool. `get_vector_full_state` and `get_vector_pulse` unaffected (the former was fixed in #2649; the latter assembles its own compact payload). Also extracted `sectionScope` / `VectorSectionScope` out of `vector-full-state-fit.ts` into `src/lib/bie/vector-fit-scope.ts` so both Vector tools share ONE scope-note convention rather than shipping a second near-copy — behaviour-neutral, proven by #2649's 13 tests passing unchanged. |
| **Regression guard** | `src/lib/largo/vector-analytics-fit.test.ts`, 12 tests: fits the budget at every `regimeDays` the clamp accepts; a payload already inside the budget is left completely untouched; `daily_regime` yields before the screener; the NEWEST regime sessions survive; real totals are reported; a preset's own counters stay honest after a trim while its screen-level denominators do not move; the ladder never trims below its floors; `events` / `latest_event` survive a pathological base; the `fit` block sits before the big sections; an `available: false` envelope passes through untouched; absent sections neither fabricate rows nor throw. A **non-vacuous premise guard** asserts both halves of the corrected measurement — over the 14,000 budget at `regimeDays = 30`, and still under the 16,000 cap — so the suite cannot pass vacuously and cannot quietly re-adopt the retracted claim. bie + largo **1385 pass / 0 fail**, tsc clean, lint clean, Node 20.20.2. |
| **Status** | FIXED. |

## 2026-08-22 — [FINDING, P2 Helix] The IV column guessed its own units per row, and rendered a degenerate solve as a plausible number — FIXED

> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Symptom** | HELIX's tape IV column and the contract drilldown drawer showed `106%` for a contract whose stored value is `106.2`, and `17%` for one storing `0.17`. Two different units rendered by one formatter, decided per row. The 4.2% of rows taking the second branch were displayed **divided by 100** — and the resulting number looks entirely ordinary, so nothing about it invites doubt. |
| **Root cause** | `fmtIv` (`src/features/helix/lib/helix-flow-format.ts`) branched `iv < 3 ? iv * 100 : iv`, i.e. it inferred fraction-vs-percent **from the value itself**. That is only sound if the feed is genuinely mixed-unit. It is not: measured over 3500 live rows carrying IV — min 0.07, p25 0.13, median 0.17, p75 0.23 — a single fractional mode with no second cluster in the tens, which is the shape a mixed-unit feed would produce. The branch therefore had nothing to disambiguate and only ever mis-scaled its own tail. |
| **Evidence** | Live production tape, 5000 rows / 168h, 2026-08-22, read-only. 3500 rows carry IV (all from the Group B / SPX-SPY writer — see `HELIX-MAP.md` §4A; the column is blank for every equity name). 3352 below the branch, **148 (4.2%) above it**. Probing what those 148 actually are was the load-bearing step: **all SPY, all expiry 2026-08-21 with `dte: -1` (EXPIRED), all deep ITM** (365C/400C/500C against a ~640 spot), mean DTE **3d** vs the body's **146d**. An expiring deep-ITM option is almost all intrinsic, so the provider's IV solve is degenerate and returns noise — 106.2, 69.24, 43.12. These are not high-IV contracts; they are non-measurements. |
| **Fix** | `fmtIv` renders the feed's real unit uniformly: `(iv * 100).toFixed(0)%`. No branch, no inference. |
| **Fix rationale** | The old branch was worse than either honest alternative, which is the point of this entry. It rendered `106.2` as **"106%"** — a plausible IV a member has no reason to distrust. In the feed's real unit the same row reads `10620%`, which is self-evidently not a measurement. Given a number that lies quietly and one that announces itself, take the second. **Deliberately NOT done:** suppressing IV where the solve is degenerate. That needs a threshold nobody has justified — real 0DTE contracts do trade at several hundred percent — and "which IV readings are meaningless" is a product question, raised for the coordinator rather than settled by a magic number in a formatter. It also overlaps the still-open §9.5, since every degenerate row is an expired contract the Expiry panel is separately mis-bucketing. |
| **Blast radius** | Two consumers of `fmtIv`, both member-facing and both fixed by the one change: `HelixFlowTable.tsx:206` (tape IV column) and `ContractDrilldownDrawer.tsx:237` (drilldown stat). `fmtIvRank` in the Night Hawk lane is an unrelated function on a different field and is untouched. Largo is unaffected — its payloads carry the raw numeric, never this rendering. |
| **Also fixed here (one-line drive-by, same lane, file I own)** | `scripts/audit/helix-tape-inventory.mjs` printed `(absent) -> OTHER` in its per-rule listing — a hardcoded label written before `UNREPORTED` existed — so the same run printed `UNREPORTED 70%` in its bucket table and `OTHER` for the identical 3500 rows two lines later. It now asks the real `executionRouteKey` for the absent case instead of hardcoding an answer. Display-only, no verdict depended on it; folded in rather than opening a PR for one string. |
| **Regression guard** | `helix-flow-format.test.ts`, 20 tests total: the unit pinned at every magnitude (0.07 → 7%, 0.17 → 17%, 2.99 → 299%, 3 → 300% — no discontinuity where the branch used to sit), the three real degenerate values pinned as obviously-wrong rather than plausible (106.2 → 10620%), and absence pinned to `—` for null/undefined/0/negative/NaN/Infinity. |
| **Status** | FIXED — **pending live validation.** The IV column must be observed on production rendering fractional values before this is closed. |

## 2026-08-22 — [FINDING, P1 Meridian] A pre-open earnings print's reaction was read open→close, dropping the premarket gap — 27% of BMO prints displayed with the WRONG SIGN — FIXED

> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Symptom** | Meridian displayed DDOG's 2026-08-06 earnings print as **+0.81%** — a small gain — on a print the stock fell **19.03%** on. Same shape on PODD 2026-08-05 (+4.11% shown, −20.12% actual), SE 2026-03-03 (+9.23% shown, −16.53% actual) and ONON 2025-11-12 (−5.31% shown, +17.99% actual). Not marginal names and not a rounding error: the number pointed the opposite way to the market. |
| **Root cause** | `reactionForPrint` (`src/lib/meridian/meridian-reaction-core.ts`) read a BMO (pre-open) print as `session_open_to_close`. A pre-open print is priced in the **premarket**, so by the time the bell rings it has already arrived as an opening **gap** — and an open→close read starts *after* that gap. This is the identical half-measurement the AMC branch was fixed for, on the other half of the function. The code even stated the wrong rationale out loud: *"a pre-open print is read open→close, because the market has that whole session to price it"* — false for a 07:00 ET release, and contradicted three lines below by the AMC branch's own comment (*"an open→close read on the anchor session would skip the gap that is the reaction"*). |
| **Why it was not caught** | The AMC fix was scoped as a fix to the *AMC* case. Its driving measurement sampled 206 **post-close** prints and never a pre-open one, so the symmetric question was never asked. Worse, the test suite **asserted the defect as correct** — `"a BMO print's reaction IS its session — the two reads must not drift apart"` pinned `reaction_pct === session_change_pct` for BMO, because open→close was the assumed-correct baseline both branches were compared *against*. |
| **Evidence** | Cohort: 519 settled BMO prints across 120 `importance>=4` tickers, 2025-08 → 2026-08 (Benzinga timings, Polygon daily bars). mean \|open→close − prior_close→close\| **4.31pp**, median 2.86, p90 **10.04**, max **30.94**; **140/519 = 27.0% carry the opposite sign**. 43.6% of all settled prints are BMO (5,211 of 11,956 over 2026-02→08). Cross-tool proof on one named print — WMT reported 2026-08-20 at **07:00:00 ET**, prior close 114.30, open 106.38, close 103.84: `get_earnings` served **−2.39%** while `get_earnings_history` served UW's independent **−9.15%** for the same print, 6.76pp apart depending on which tool Largo called. |
| **Fix** | A print with a KNOWN bell-relative timing is priced while the market is shut, so both branches now read `prior_close_to_close`; they differ only in WHICH close precedes the print (AMC → the report date's own; BMO → the close of the session before it, via a new `prevSessionYmd`). A mid-session (`unknown`) print is the one case with no gap to catch and keeps `session_open_to_close`. Where no prior close exists the reaction is **null**, never a silent fallback to open→close — the same refusal the AMC branch already makes. |
| **Before / after, live** | `WMT 2026-08-20 −2.39 → −9.15` (now matches UW exactly) · `DDOG 2026-08-06 +0.81 → −19.03` · `PODD 2026-08-05 +4.11 → −20.12` · `SE 2026-03-03 +9.23 → −16.53` · `ONON 2025-11-12 −5.31 → +17.99` · `MSFT 2026-07-29 (AMC) 15.51 → 15.51` unchanged. |
| **Fix rationale — and what was deliberately NOT chosen** | A third candidate was measured, not assumed: anchor to the last trade **before the print time** (extended-hours minute bars), isolating the print from unrelated overnight drift. Rejected. On 90 prints, **47 had no premarket trade before the print at all**, so it is undefined half the time, and where premarket volume is thin one small trade would anchor the headline number — trading a known ~4pp bias for an unbounded, invisible one. What it did establish is that `prior_close_to_close` carries a **real residual**: on the 43 prints where the premarket read is independent the two differ by a median **1.18pp** (p90 4.10) and disagree in sign on **9.3%**. That residual is genuine pre-print drift attributed to the print, so it is **disclosed on the value** as `reaction_includes_prior_drift` rather than left to be discovered (`_COMMON.md` §7). |
| **Blast radius** | Everything downstream of `reaction_pct` for a BMO print: `MeridianEarningsHistoryPanel` (implied-vs-realized was comparing an implied *move* against a partial one), `MeridianEarningsIntelPanel`, `MeridianEarningsTabs`, `printHistorySummary`'s "avg reaction", and `get_earnings` / `get_meridian_event` at the Largo boundary. `session_change_pct` is unchanged and still reported under its own name. The sibling trap was re-checked at the same time and is clean: `barLimitForWindow` is used at **both** surviving call sites in `meridian-reaction.ts` and no other caller exists. |
| **Regression guard** | `meridian-reaction-core.test.ts` — the test that encoded the defect is replaced by its mirror image ("a BMO reaction contains the PREMARKET gap — an open→close read INVERTS its sign too"), plus one asserting BMO and AMC now share a measure and differ only in basis (so the fix cannot be undone on one branch alone, which is how this happened the first time), plus the no-prior-session null case. `meridian-open-session.test.ts` updated for the new BMO measure, keeping its settled/provisional intent intact. **497 pass / 0 fail** across all 39 Meridian test files on Node 20.20.2; tsc clean. |
| **Status** | FIXED. |

## 2026-08-22 — [FINDING, P2 Helix] An absent GEX wall badge meant three different things, and the commonest was "we never looked" — FIXED

> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Symptom** | A HELIX tape print with no FLIP / C WALL / P WALL badge reads, to a member and to Largo, as "this strike is not near a key gamma level". For most prints that is not what it meant. The same absence also covered "the GEX lookup timed out" and "this ticker was never evaluated at all", and nothing in the payload could tell the three apart. |
| **Root cause** | `enrichFlowsWithGex` (`src/lib/flow-gex-enrichment.ts`) returned the row **unchanged** when it had no levels for that ticker, and `enrichFlowWithGex` returned it unchanged when the strike matched no level. Two different facts, one indistinguishable encoding — absence. The ticker can be missing from the map for two independent reasons: it fell past the `maxTickers = 100` enrichment cap, or its `getGexLevelsForTicker` call hit the 300 ms timeout / returned nothing. |
| **Evidence** | Live production tape, 5000 rows / 168h, 2026-08-22, via `scripts/audit/helix-tape-inventory.mjs`. The page spans **273 distinct tickers against a cap of 100 — 173 never evaluated** — and `gex_proximity` is present on **2.2%** of rows (3.9% Group A, 1.5% Group B). So the overwhelmingly dominant meaning of a missing badge is *never checked*, not *not near a level*. |
| **Fix** | Every enriched row now carries **`gex_evaluated: boolean`**, set **explicitly on both branches**: `true` whenever real levels were in hand and the comparison was made — including when the answer is "not near anything", because "checked, not near" is a known state — and `false` when the print was never looked up. `FlowAlert` documents it; `tool-defs.ts` teaches Largo to read it before drawing anything from an absent label, with the measured 2.2% figure so the model knows absence is the norm rather than the exception. |
| **Fix rationale** | Explicit `false` rather than an omitted key, per contract C3: a known state must never be encoded as absence, and `undefined` would read as "unknown" — which is the very ambiguity being removed. Deliberately NOT done: raising the 100-ticker cap. That trades upstream cost against coverage and wants its own measurement (each lookup is 300 ms-bounded and 60 s-cached, but 273 concurrent is a different fan-out from 100); disclosing the gap is the honest first step, widening it is a separate decision. The badge rendering is also unchanged — a member still sees no badge; what changed is that the payload can now say why. |
| **Blast radius** | `enrichFlowWithGex` (SSE path, `/api/market/flows/stream`) and `enrichFlowsWithGex` (REST path + warmers), so both tape paths. Enriched rows ride into `get_ecosystem_context`'s `flow_full_state`, which is why `tool-defs.ts` is updated in the same change. `flowSignals` and `gexProximityLabel` still key off `gex_proximity` alone and are untouched — the flag is additive. |
| **Also done here** | The cap decision was extracted to a pure `tickersToEvaluate()` in `flow-gex-proximity.ts`. `flow-gex-enrichment.ts` reaches `server-only`, so **nothing in it can be imported by a test** — the same constraint that forced `helix-tape-analytics.ts` out of `product-reads.ts`, and precisely how a cap this consequential stayed unmeasured. The helper also returns `skipped`, so a caller can state how many tickers it passed over instead of discovering the shortfall as silent absence. |
| **Regression guard** | `src/lib/flow-gex-proximity.test.ts`, 9 tests (the file had none): the at/near thresholds and flip-outranks-walls precedence, refusal to compare against levels it does not have, `gex_evaluated: true` on the not-near branch, no mutation of the input print, and four on the cap — the split at the boundary, a cap above the ticker count skipping nothing, zero/negative/NaN caps evaluating nothing while still naming what they skipped, and blank tickers not counting against the cap. |
| **Status** | FIXED — **pending live validation.** `gex_evaluated: false` must be observed on production rows whose ticker is past the cap before this is closed. |

## 2026-08-23 — [FINDING, P1 SPX Slayer] Members see "96% conviction" on every play — `confidence` is a CONSTANT rendered as a per-play score, 51/51 — MEASURED (member-facing fix pending coordinator)

> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Symptom** | The SPX Slayer desk renders `` `${confidence}% conviction` `` per play. Measured across **every closed play in production — 51 of 51 over 54.3 days — the value is 96.** Not usually, not approximately: identically 96, zero variance. A member reading "96% conviction" reasonably takes it as this setup's assessed strength; it is what every committed play says, and has said for at least eight weeks. |
| **Root cause** | `src/features/spx/lib/spx-signals.ts:706` — `clamp(Math.round(abs * 1.15 + factors.length * 3), 0, 96)`. The `factors.length * 3` term is the mechanism: the desk routinely produces 8–14 factors, so it contributes 24–42 points on its own. Against entry thresholds of `playFullMinScore()` **52** / `playStarterMinScore()` **48** / `playColdBuyMinScore()` **78**, anything clearing the gate lands at or above the clamp ceiling. At the cold-buy threshold it takes **3 factors** to saturate; at full-entry, 13. Empirically every committed play saturates. |
| **Evidence** | `node scripts/audit/spx-confidence-calibration.mjs` against production `/api/market/spx/outcomes?limit=200` (read-only, cron-bearer auth): 51 closed plays, `informationCheck` → `distinct_values: 1, constant: 96`. Bucketed calibration puts all 51 in the 96–100 bucket (55% realized win rate) and **0 in every other bucket**. A point-biserial against it is `0/0`; the harness returns a **degenerate** verdict rather than `NaN`, because `NaN` reads as "no signal found" when the finding is "the input never varies". |
| **Correction to the 2026-08-22 `confidence` entry (#2646)** | That entry described the field as "uncalibrated" and noted the count term "counts conflicting factors as confidence". **Both true but understated.** The sharper fact — that at the commit threshold it is always exactly 96, so it is a constant rather than a weak signal — was not measured then and is materially worse. The Largo-boundary omission #2646 shipped remains correct and sufficient for *that* surface; what it did not do, and what its write-up implied was merely imprecise rather than vacuous, is the member-facing number. |
| **Also correcting my own advice** | #2646's `confidence_omitted` message tells the model to "use `score`, `grade`, and `agreeing` vs `weighted_conflicts` to judge conviction instead". Measured on the same 51 plays: `r(|score|, win) = 0.172`, `r(grade_rank, win) = −0.038`. So `score` carries weak positive signal and **`grade` carries none in this sample**. n=51 is small and neither number is established — but I should not have implied those substitutes were validated, and that text overstates them. |
| **Fix** | **Measurement + harness only in this PR.** `scripts/audit/spx-confidence-calibration.mjs` makes the question reproducible; `scripts/audit/lib/calibration-eval.mjs` carries the pure helpers. The member-facing change — stop rendering a constant as a per-play percentage — is **deliberately not made here**: the coordinator directed on #2646 that the UI number be left alone pending a calibrated replacement, and that direction was given when the field was believed merely uncalibrated. The new evidence changes the input to that decision, so it goes back to them rather than being acted on unilaterally. |
| **Blast radius** | Member UI (`computeSpxTradeSignal`'s `"{n}% conviction"` headline and every surface rendering `play.confidence`). The Largo boundary is already covered by #2646. The stored `confidence` column on the outcomes ledger is likewise 96 for all 51 rows, so **historical rows carry no recoverable conviction signal** — any future calibration must be built from `score`/`grade`/factors, not from this field's history. |
| **Regression guard** | `scripts/audit/lib/calibration-eval.test.mjs`, 9 tests. The load-bearing one: a constant predictor returns a **degenerate verdict rather than a number**. Also empty buckets reporting `win_rate: null` not `0` (0% is a measurement), and thin buckets flagged `insufficient_sample` rather than rendered as an actionable percentage. |
| **Status** | MEASURED. Harness shipped. **Member-facing fix awaiting the coordinator's decision**, with evidence and options on the PR. |

## 2026-08-22 — [FINDING, P2 Helix] The Route Breakdown panel bucketed 98.8% of the tape as "OTHER" — and counted 3500 prints with no route as a measured one — FIXED

> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Symptom** | HELIX's Route Breakdown panel (`/flows`, kicker "◇ execution") renders one bar reading **OTHER, 98.8%**, with FLOOR at 1.2% and SWEEP at 0.1%. Four of its six configured buckets — **BLOCK, SPLIT, CROSS, MULTI — never fire at all**. A panel whose answer is "other" for 98.8% of prints is not a breakdown, and it reads as a broken feed rather than as a vocabulary gap. The same aggregate ships to Largo as `route_breakdown`, so the model was being told that 98.8% of institutional flow has an unknown execution route. |
| **Root cause** | Two independent causes, both in `src/features/helix/lib/helix-flow-format.ts`. **(1) Vocabulary gap:** `executionRouteKey` scanned `alert_rule` for six words (`SWEEP/BLOCK/SPLIT/CROSS/FLOOR/MULTI`). The live tape's dominant rule family is `RepeatedHits` / `RepeatedHitsAscendingFill` / `RepeatedHitsDescendingFill` — **28.7% of all prints** — which contains none of them, so all of it fell to `OTHER`. `ruleLabel`, **fourteen lines above in the same file**, already mapped `"repeated"` to a `REPEAT` badge rendered on that same tape. Two functions parsed one field with different word lists, and the panel used the one that did not know the most common value. **(2) Absence published as measurement:** `executionRouteKey` returned `OTHER` for a print carrying **no `alert_rule` at all**, which is 70% of the tape — every row from the second writer documented in `HELIX-MAP.md` §4A (an SPX/SPY-only feed that sends no rule field). `OTHER` asserts we looked and found something else; for 3500 prints we had never had a route to look at. |
| **Evidence** | Live production member tape, 5000 rows / 168h, read-only via the new `scripts/audit/helix-tape-inventory.mjs` (2026-08-22). Buckets: `OTHER 4939 (98.8%)`, `FLOOR 58 (1.2%)`, `SWEEP 3 (0.1%)`; BLOCK/SPLIT/CROSS/MULTI absent. The nine distinct `alert_rule` values present: `(absent) 3500 (70.0%)`, `RepeatedHits 962 (19.2%)`, `RepeatedHitsAscendingFill 280 (5.6%)`, `RepeatedHitsDescendingFill 197 (3.9%)`, `FloorTradeLargeCap 23`, `LowHistoricVolumeFloor 23`, `FloorTradeMidCap 10`, `SweepsFollowedByFloor 3`, `FloorTradeSmallCap 2`. Reproduce with `node --import tsx scripts/audit/helix-tape-inventory.mjs`. |
| **Fix** | One shared `ALERT_RULE_WORDS` set both readers draw from, with **deliberately different precedence** because they answer different questions: the BADGE asks *which rule fired* (`REPEAT` first — already shipped to members), the PANEL asks *how the order executed* (mechanisms first, `REPEAT` last, since "repeated hits" is a pattern across prints, not an execution mechanism). Adds `GRENADE` to the panel and `SPLIT`/`CROSS`/`MULTI` to the shared set. `executionRouteKey` now returns three distinguishable outcomes: a word, `OTHER` (rule present, names nothing we know), and **`UNREPORTED`** (no rule on the print at all). The panel gives `UNREPORTED` a deliberately muted colour and a `title` hint so it reads as a gap in the data rather than a competing category; `tool-defs.ts` teaches Largo the same distinction. |
| **Blast radius** | Exactly two consumers of `executionRouteKey`, both fixed by the shared root cause: `src/features/helix/components/RouteBreakdown.tsx:33` (member panel) and `src/lib/largo/helix-tape-analytics.ts:88` (`routeBreakdown`, served as `get_helix_tape_analytics.route_breakdown`). `ruleLabel` has one consumer, the tape badge, whose output is **unchanged** for every live rule value. No print that already had an execution route changes bucket — the mechanism words keep their original order. |
| **Fix rationale** | An earlier draft of this change collapsed both readers onto one precedence and flipped `RepeatedHitsSweep` from `SWEEP` to `REPEAT` in the panel. That was **wrong** and the existing Largo test caught it: it "fixed" a disagreement that is not a defect, and it would have quietly redefined an execution panel as a rule-family panel without anyone deciding to. Corrected to share the word SET but not the ORDER. Deliberately NOT changed: the SWEEP-before-FLOOR precedence for `SweepsFollowedByFloor` (3 rows — real ambiguity, negligible impact, and changing it would be a second issue); and the deeper product question of whether a panel titled "Route Breakdown" should bucket alert-rule families at all is written up for the coordinator rather than decided here. |
| **Regression guard** | `helix-flow-format.test.ts`, 17 tests: the eight live `alert_rule` values each pinned to their bucket with an explicit assertion that **none may land in `OTHER`**; absence (`undefined`/`null`/`""`/whitespace) pinned to `UNREPORTED`; a present-but-unknown rule pinned to `OTHER`; mechanism-beats-pattern pinned for Sweep/Block/Floor; and a drift test asserting **both readers draw from the same word set**, which is the guarantee that re-opening the 28.7% gap fails loudly. Full suite 10075/10075 on Node 20.20.2; tsc clean; `lint:brand` clean. |
| **Status** | FIXED — **pending live validation.** Merged is not done: the panel must be observed on production showing a real bucket distribution with `UNREPORTED` present, and `get_helix_tape_analytics.route_breakdown` must be observed carrying the new buckets, before this is closed. |

## 2026-08-22 — [FINDING, P1 Vector/Largo] `get_vector_full_state` shipped the whole bead rail into a 16,000-char transport, so the model received ~0.1% of it — and the cut landed on the freshness and absence blocks — FIXED

> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Symptom** | During RTH, `get_vector_full_state` (and `get_ecosystem_context.vector_full_state`, which promises "the exact same object") delivered the model a fraction of one percent of its payload. The model still received spot, walls, flip, magnet and the play — a fluent, plausible desk read — with **no absence report and no freshness block**, because those sit last in key order. Nothing errored and nothing looked wrong from the outside; this is the same silent shape as #2433 / #2436 / #2480. |
| **Root cause** | `vectorFullStateForLargo` (`src/lib/largo/product-reads.ts`) returned `fetchVectorFullState`'s object verbatim, and that object carries the ENTIRE in-process bead rail — `getVectorWallHistory` returns every sample, and Vector records `VECTOR_WALL_NODES_PER_SIDE = 20` levels per side on **both** lenses with a `notional` on each, so one oracle bead serializes to **~4,077 chars**, a quarter of the whole budget. `anthropicToolLoop` caps every `tool_result` at `MAX_TOOL_RESULT_CHARS = 16_000` and enforces it with `raw.slice(0, MAX)` — a **head** slice, so key order decides what survives. `computeVectorFullState` places `wallHistory` near the end and `withReadContext` spreads `...state` FIRST and appends its blocks after it, so the cut landed inside the rail and discarded, in order: `wallEvents`, `vexWalls`, `vexFlip`, `darkPoolLevels`, `unavailable_sections`, `wall_history_empty_reason`, `observed_at`, `observed_session_date`, `as_of`, `session_date`, `age_seconds`, `freshness`, `note`. **Every disclosure this lane built so the model is never misled was appended last, and was therefore the first thing the transport ate.** |
| **Evidence** | Measured offline against the committed `VECTOR_FULL_STATE_FIXTURE` with realistic synthetic oracle rails (20 levels/side, both lenses): 12 beads (1 min @5s) = 52,586 chars, **3.3×** the cap, model receives 30.4%; 60 beads = 248,330 (15.5×, 6.4%); 360 beads (30 min) = 1,471,730 (**92×**, 1.1%); 3,720 beads — SPX's real post-compaction shape per `compactHistoryToCap` — = 15,173,810 (**948×**, **0.11%**); 5,760 (`MAX_HISTORY`) = 23,492,930 (1,468×, 0.07%). **The payload leaves the budget after roughly four beads — about twenty seconds of oracle rail.** |
| **Why no prior audit caught it** | It is invisible off-hours. Outside RTH the rail is empty, the payload is small, and every Vector tool returns COMPLETE — so an off-hours `largo-truncation-probe.mjs` run is not merely weak evidence here, it is affirmatively misleading. The defect only exists on a moving tape. |
| **Fix** | New `src/lib/bie/vector-full-state-fit.ts` — `fitVectorFullStateForModel`, built on the existing `fit-tool-result.ts` (`LARGO_RESULT_CHAR_BUDGET` = 14,000). Every scalar and every disclosure field passes through **verbatim** and is placed BEFORE the trimmable sections; the four unbounded lists are sampled in descending order of information-per-byte (`wallEvents` → `ladder.rows` → `flowMarkers.prints` → `wallHistory`), each measured against the WHOLE assembled object, each carrying a `fit.<section>` scope with `returned` / `total` / `truncated` / `note`. King strikes are force-retained in the ladder; both time series are kept newest-first and returned in their documented ascending order. Applied at BOTH `vectorFullStateForLargo` and `ecosystem-context.ts`. Fixed at the source, never by raising the cap. |
| **Fix rationale** | The fit is at the TOOL boundary, deliberately not in `computeVectorFullState`: `buildPulseSignalsForState` diffs the whole rail to detect pulse signals, `scoreTopWalls` reads it for the persistence factor, and `eventsFromWallHistory` derives the narration from all of it — trimming there would silently change what those derivations see. Keeping the composer full is also what makes the scope note *true*: every derived field really was computed over the entire rail, which is why the note tells the model to cite those rather than count visible rows. `wallHistory` is sampled last because it is the least information-dense section — its content is already summarized by `wallEvents` and `wallIntegrity`. |
| **Blast radius** | Two model-facing call sites, both fixed: `get_vector_full_state` and `get_ecosystem_context.vector_full_state`. `get_vector_pulse` is **not** affected — `vectorPulseForLargo` assembles its own compact payload (signals capped at 25, no rail); verified, not assumed. The internal composers that call `fetchVectorFullState` directly (`slash-prompts.ts`, `mini-panel.ts`, `desk-scope-prefetch.ts`) are unchanged and still receive the full state, which is correct — they extract specific fields rather than shipping the object to a model. Two tool descriptions updated so the model is told to read `fit.<section>.total` and never to count visible rows. **Sibling, NOT fixed here:** `get_vector_analytics` is at ~93% of the cap at default parameters and ~102% at the `regimeDays = 30` its own clamp accepts — a P3 recorded in `VECTOR-MAP.md` §6 and queued behind this. |
| **Regression guard** | `src/lib/bie/vector-full-state-fit.test.ts`, 13 tests: the payload fits at every rail length including a full session AND `MAX_TOOL_RESULT_CHARS`; the disclosure fields survive a 3,720-bead rail; scalars and derived reads pass through untouched; `fit.wall_history.total` is the REAL rail length; an untruncated section says "All N" and an empty one says "No …" rather than "All 0"; beads are the most recent and stay ascending; both king strikes survive a 202-row ladder trim; `flowMarkers.meta` survives while its prints are sampled; a null ladder stays null; and the fit degrades to scalars rather than throwing when even the base is over budget. A **non-vacuous premise guard** asserts the UNFITTED state really does exceed the cap, so the suite cannot pass by the defect having quietly gone away. Two pre-existing tests that pinned the old "returns the state verbatim" invariant were updated to pin the new one — `ecosystem-context.test.ts` now asserts the field equals `fitVectorFullStateForModel(FIXTURE)`, which is *stronger* than "verbatim": it makes the two paths provably unable to drift apart, which is what the "exact same object" contract actually promises. `vector-analytics-wiring.test.ts`'s source-assert now requires the fitted call and forbids the raw return. bie + largo suites 1367/1367, tsc clean, lint clean, Node 20.20.2. |
| **Status** | FIXED. Live confirmation with `largo-truncation-probe.mjs` is OWED and must run **during RTH** — an off-hours run cannot see this defect. Largo was additionally confirmed down platform-wide when this shipped, so no live-response verification was attempted. |

## 2026-08-22 — [FINDING, P3 Vector/ops] `vector-alerts` sat in the coverage audit's "silently dark" bucket, and an in-code comment stated its closed-tab delivery as a live guarantee — FIXED

> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Symptom** | `scripts/audit/cron-schedule-coverage.mjs` listed `vector-alerts` under *"UNSCHEDULED AND UNEXPLAINED — a feature may be silently dark"*, alongside seven other lanes' routes. Its own message warns why that matters: *"Leaving it unlisted is how helix-signal-outcomes stayed dark."* |
| **Root cause** | Two independent facts, both verified 2026-08-22, neither written down anywhere a reader would find them. (1) `vector-alerts` has **no deployed EventBridge rule** — `blackout-infra/terraform/modules/crons/cron-jobs.json` @ `68a0aa0f` carries 39 rules and Vector holds four of them (`walls-warm`, `universe-snapshot`, `full-state-snapshot`, `dark-pool-warm`); the route's `railway.vector-alerts.toml` is dead config, since Railway no longer exists. (2) **`VECTOR_ALERTS_PUSH` is not present** in `blackout-production/app/env` (98 keys, checked by key name only), so the route returns `{ok: true, inert: true}` even when called by hand. Scheduling it today would change nothing. |
| **Why this is P3 and not P1** | No member-facing promise is broken. `VectorAlertsPanel`'s own tooltip offers delivery only *"while this tab is in the background"* — never closed-tab — and the in-page toast, the panel history and the desk terminal all still fire from the client-side `evaluateAlerts` on every live tick. The feature a member can actually see works. What was wrong was the **record**: an unexplained entry in a list whose whole job is to separate "dark by accident" from "dark on purpose" trains readers to skim the list, which is how a genuinely broken row in it gets missed. |
| **The part that would have misled an engineer** | `VectorPageShell.persistRules` mirrors every member's rules to Postgres and its comment read *"The mirrored copy is what `/api/cron/vector-alerts` reads to fire push alerts to a closed tab."* Stated as live behaviour. Anyone reading that — while debugging a member's "I didn't get my alert" report, say — would have concluded the delivery path exists and gone looking for a bug in it. |
| **Fix** | (a) `vector-alerts` added to `INTENTIONALLY_UNSCHEDULED` in `cron-schedule-coverage.mjs` with both reasons and the pointer to `VECTOR-MAP.md` §7; it now prints under "Intentionally unscheduled" and the unexplained bucket drops to seven routes, all other lanes'. (b) The `persistRules` comment rewritten to say what is actually true — the cron is dormant on two counts, nothing member-facing depends on it, and the mirror is still worth writing because it makes turning the feature on a config decision rather than a rebuild. |
| **What was deliberately NOT done** | The alternative remedy — deploy the rule and set `VECTOR_ALERTS_PUSH` — is a product decision (a new member-facing push channel), not an audit fix, and is explicitly not taken here. VAPID is fully configured and `GEX_ALERTS_PUSH = 1`, so the platform push channel itself is live and in use by another product; Vector's is the one that is off. Raised with the coordinator, who chose (a). |
