| **Blast radius** | The audit script and one comment. No behaviour change: no schedule added, no flag set, no route touched. The remaining unexplained routes belong to other lanes (`darkpool-discord`, `helix-discord-digest`, `helix-signal-outcomes`, `largo-morning-brief`, `meridian-warm`, `thermal-discord`, `welcome-sequence`, `zerodte-grade`) and are deliberately left for their owners. |
| **Regression guard** | The coverage audit is itself the guard and is self-checking: removing the entry returns `vector-alerts` to the unexplained bucket. Verified before and after against the deployed manifest. |
| **Status** | FIXED (the record). The dormant feature itself remains dormant, deliberately, and is OPEN as a product question. |

## 2026-08-23 — [FINDING, P2 SPX Slayer] `production_eligible: "not_started"` on all 14 playbooks reads as a safety gate and gates nothing — while the production playbook gate is ON — FIXED (made explicit + ratcheted)

> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Symptom** | `PLAYBOOK_SURFACE_STATUS` marks every one of the 14 playbooks `production_eligible: "not_started"`, and `PLAYBOOK-ARCHITECTURE-STATUS.md` §6 renders that as a **"Prod eligible"** column reading `not_started` for all 14. Both read as "no playbook can run in production yet". Meanwhile `PLAYBOOK_LIVE_GATE="1"` in production means gate A17 **requires** a matched primary playbook before any BUY — so playbooks decide live entries today. |
| **Root cause** | The field is descriptive and always was. Measured at `9b20b63c`: **nothing outside `playbook-implementation-status.ts` reads `production_eligible`, or `PLAYBOOK_SURFACE_STATUS` at all.** It is a fact that exists in the system and is not wired to any rule — the defect class this fleet keeps finding, in its documentation-shaped form. |
| **Evidence** | `grep -rn "production_eligible" src/ --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx'` returns only the defining file; same for `PLAYBOOK_SURFACE_STATUS`. Production config read from `blackout-production/app/env` (named non-secret keys only): `PLAYBOOK_LIVE_GATE = "1"`, `PLAYBOOK_LIVE_ALLOWLIST` unset. |
| **Why it is not cosmetic** | A reader who trusts it de-prioritises real production defects in this subsystem. That is close to what happened with PB-01/PB-02 (#2636): had the "Prod eligible: not_started" column been taken at face value, "two playbooks cannot fire in production" reads as expected rather than as a P1. The same document also states *"Prod — playbook live gate **off** unless `PLAYBOOK_LIVE_GATE=1`"*, which is literally true and practically inverted, since it **is** `1`. |
| **Fix** | Deliberately NOT wiring it — wiring `not_started` as written would block all 14 playbooks and stop the engine entering at all, which is a behaviour change requiring the coordinator's decision, not a lane's. Instead: (a) a prominent comment at the constant stating it is descriptive, gates nothing, and naming the tension with `PLAYBOOK_LIVE_GATE=1`; (b) `playbook-status-doc-sync.test.ts` pins the current values so a future change to gating or to these statuses must come past that comment; (c) all eleven playbook docs bannered with the environment claims that are false. **Open question raised to the coordinator on the PR: should `production_eligible` gate?** |
| **Blast radius** | The doc audit that surfaced this covered all eleven `docs/spx/PLAYBOOK-*.md`. Result recorded in `SLAYER-MAP.md` §6.4: they are **accurate about the code and false about the world** — §6's 70-cell matrix, §16's constants and §17's code map all verified correct, while all eleven reference decommissioned staging (~154 times), the "Single Source of Truth" header names a repo that is not this one (`blackout-web-sandbox`), a host deleted 2026-07-25, and a "Railway prod" that does not exist, and §18 calls `npm run validate:staging-playbook`, removed from `package.json`. |
| **Regression guard** | `src/features/spx/lib/playbook-status-doc-sync.test.ts`, 3 tests: §6's matrix matches `PLAYBOOK_SURFACE_STATUS` cell-for-cell; every registered playbook appears in the doc (no silent omission); and the parse must find exactly 14 rows, so a regex that matches nothing FAILS rather than passing vacuously — the absence-reads-as-clean trap. SPX lib suite 660/660, tsc clean, on Node 20.20.2. |
| **Status** | FIXED (made explicit + ratcheted). The gating question is open with the coordinator. |

## 2026-08-23 — [FINDING, P1 Largo] The grounding caveat never rendered as a caveat, the timeframe caveat rendered as "Note", and the cron could not tell a disclosed answer from a silent one — one root cause, three drifts — FIXED

> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Symptom** | Three separate honesty signals degraded on the way to the member, all from the same cause. (1) The **grounding** caveat — the one that says the answer's own numbers could not be traced to data pulled this turn — reached the reader as italic prose buried mid-answer, never as the distinct callout the UI has had wired for it the whole time. (2) The **timeframe** caveat rendered under the generic label **"Note"** instead of "Timeframe note". (3) `auditLargoAnswerGrounding`'s "already disclosed" check could **never** fire, so the cron re-flagged every low-coverage answer as undisclosed — including ones a member had already been warned about. |
| **Root cause** | The strings the producers WRITE and the patterns the consumers LOOK FOR were two hand-kept lists with nothing binding them, and they had drifted three ways. `applyVerificationCaveat` emitted `_Data check: …_` while `answer-caveats.ts` collects only trailing `> **Heading.**` blocks and its `verification` pattern waits for `> **Grounding note.**` — a kind, a regex and a "Grounding note" label all wired end to end for a string **nothing in the codebase ever produced**. `applyPlanCaveat` emitted `> **Timeframe caveat.**` against a matcher expecting `Timeframe note.`, so it fell to the `other` fallback. And `LARGO_RUNTIME_CAUTION_MARKER` was `"BIE verification"`, which no producer emitted either. |
| **Evidence** | Measured by running each REAL producer through the REAL matcher on this tree, before the fix: `verification → kinds=[]` (not split off at all), `plan → kinds=[other]`, `coherence → kinds=[coherence]` ✓, `source-conflict → kinds=[source-conflict]` ✓. And for the marker: `LARGO_RUNTIME_CAUTION_MARKER = "BIE verification"`, `caveat contains marker? false`, `auditLargoAnswerGrounding(caveatedAnswer).shouldFlag = true` — a disclosure re-flagged as undisclosed. |
| **Fix** | `applyVerificationCaveat` emits a trailing blockquote, building its heading FROM `LARGO_RUNTIME_CAUTION_MARKER` rather than writing it out; the constant's value becomes `"Grounding note"`, which is simultaneously what the UI matcher keys on and what the cron auditor searches for. One constant, one producer, two consumers. `applyPlanCaveat` aligned to `> **Timeframe note.**`, matching both its matcher and its rendered label. |
| **Blast radius** | Every Largo answer that earns a grounding or timeframe caveat, on both the streaming and non-streaming paths, in the terminal and the Concrete renderer (`LargoAnswerMessage`, `LargoConcreteAnswer` both call `splitAnswerCaveats`). Plus the `data-correctness` cron's Largo grounding audit. The coherence, provenance, source-conflict and integrity caveats were already correct and are unchanged. |
| **Fix rationale** | Fixed the PRODUCERS to match the consumers rather than widening the regexes, because the UI's labels ("Grounding note", "Timeframe note") are the intended vocabulary and loosening a matcher to accept both spellings would have preserved the drift while hiding it. Deliberately NOT done: extracting all five caveat headings into a shared constants module. That is a five-producer refactor across the server/client boundary, and the behavioural round-trip test below pins the same property without one — a test that fails on real disagreement beats a refactor that merely makes disagreement less likely. Noted for the coordinator instead. |
| **Regression guard** | `src/features/largo/answer/caveat-round-trip.test.ts` (new, 8 tests): each real producer is invoked with a triggering input and run through the real `splitAnswerCaveats`, asserting its kind; no producer may classify as the `other` fallback; the grounding caveat is a blockquote and not italics; the cron sees a disclosed answer as disclosed **while still flagging an undisclosed one** (so the fix did not blind it); and clean input produces no caveat. Behavioural, not a source-scrape, so it survives rewording and fails only on real disagreement. **The guard was proven to fire**: reverting the plan heading failed 2 tests, reverting the grounding caveat to italics failed 3, and restoring both returned 8/8 — checked because an inert guard was already written and caught once earlier this session. |
| **Secondary finding** | The test guarding the disclosure branch — `largo-grounding-fixture.test.ts`, *"skips answers that already carry the runtime caution footer"* — **never exercised it.** Its fixture (`"SPX at 9999 with fake levels."` + a hand-written footer) yields exactly ONE numeric claim, and `shouldFlag` requires `total >= 4`, so it short-circuited on the threshold and never reached `alreadyDisclosed`. It passed, and would have passed with the disclosure check deleted outright — verified by disabling that line and watching it stay green. Rebuilt with four-plus untraceable claims and the footer produced by the REAL `applyVerificationCaveat` instead of a hand-copied string; it now fails when the check is disabled. Hand-copying the footer is what let the fixture go on asserting a format the producer had long since stopped emitting — the same drift as the defect above, one layer down. |
| **Status** | FIXED — **pending live validation.** The callout cannot be observed on production until the upstream Anthropic credit outage clears and Largo completes turns again; a low-coverage answer must then be seen rendering a distinct "Grounding note" callout rather than an italic line in the prose. |

## 2026-08-22 — [FINDING, P1 SPX Slayer/Largo] SPX Slayer's `confidence` reached the model as a formula over a FACTOR COUNT — fabricated certainty ranked against other lanes' measured scores — FIXED

> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Symptom** | Largo received `confidence: <n>` for SPX Slayer on four different paths and could rank it against products that measure theirs. `get_spx_play`'s tool description explicitly advertised the field, so the model was told to expect a confidence and handed an invented one. |
| **Root cause** | `src/features/spx/lib/spx-signals.ts:706` — `clamp(Math.round(abs * 1.15 + factors.length * 3), 0, 96)`. No realized outcome, no denominator, no calibration set. Two defects sit inside it independent of calibration: (1) `factors.length` counts **conflicting** factors — `factors` holds both signs, so contradiction cannot lower the number on its own, and the engine computes `agreeing` and `weighted_conflicts` on the very next lines and uses neither; (2) gates never revise it — `confidence` is fixed before `evaluatePlayGates` runs, so a play held by four gates reports the same conviction as one that passed clean. `docs/audit/LARGO-PRODUCT-CONTRACT.md` requires `confidence` be OMITTED when a product cannot calibrate it, "because an invented score is compared against another lane's measured one." |
| **Evidence** | Emission points traced at `50ef24e`: `run-tool.ts:1564` returned the `SpxConfluence` object verbatim; `run-tool.ts:960` returned `getSpxPlayState()`, whose payload carries the same value at top level (12 assignment sites in `spx-play-engine.ts`, all beside `available/phase/action/direction/grade/score`); `ecosystem-context.ts:847` re-served that object as `spx_full_state`; and `largo-live-feed.ts:784` **explicitly whitelisted** `confidence: play.confidence` into the live feed the model reads. `tool-defs.ts:217` listed "confidence" among the fields `get_spx_play` returns. |
| **Fix** | New `src/lib/largo/spx-confidence-boundary.ts`: `omitUncalibratedSpxConfidence()` drops the key and replaces it with `confidence_omitted`, a sentence naming why it is absent **and what to read instead** (`score`, `grade`, `agreeing` vs `weighted_conflicts`). Applied at all four emission points. Both tool descriptions now state the omission, so the model does not read the absence as a failed read. |
| **Blast radius** | All four Largo-boundary paths are covered — fixing only `get_spx_confluence` (the originally-scoped one) would have left three open doors to the same number, including the live feed, which no tool call is needed to reach. **Deliberately NOT a deep/recursive strip:** `get_ecosystem_context` nests Vector, Thermal and HELIX beside the SPX state, and removing a peer lane's *measured* confidence to fix ours would be the same defect in the other direction — a regression test asserts a nested peer's confidence survives. **Member-facing UI unchanged:** the desk still renders "{n}% conviction". That surface is a separate decision with its own blast radius, and shipping a second invented number while a calibrated one is built would repeat the mistake. |
| **Fix rationale** | Omission over a quick reformulation: a calibrated replacement must be built from `spx-play-outcomes` and validated out-of-sample, which is its own work. Omission is honest today; a hastily "improved" formula would still be uncalibrated and would look more trustworthy. The absence is NAMED rather than blank per `_COMMON.md` rule 7 — an unexplained missing field reads as a broken read, which is its own wrong answer. |
| **Also found, NOT fixed here** | `spx-play-engine.ts:1633` — `confidence: closedConfluence?.confidence ?? 0` on the session-closed path. A `0` reads as a measured floor ("0% confidence"), not as "unknown"; that is absence published as measurement, in the member payload. Logged to `docs/spx/SLAYER-MAP.md` §8 rather than fixed here: it is member-facing engine behaviour, not the Largo boundary, and belongs with the calibrated-confidence work. |
| **Regression guard** | `src/lib/largo/spx-confidence-boundary.test.ts`, 6 tests: strip + named absence, the reason text naming every substitute field, untouched pass-through for a payload that never carried `confidence` (identity-equal, no needless copy), null/undefined/primitive/array pass-through, the non-recursion guarantee protecting peer lanes, and a regression asserting against the REAL engine that `confidence` is exactly `\|score\|*1.15 + factors.length*3` — a factor count, not a measurement. `ecosystem-context.test.ts`'s two full-fidelity guards updated to build their expectation FROM the fixture (drop one key, add one), so trimming any OTHER field still fails them. Largo + BIE suites **1360/1360**, SPX lib **657/657**, tsc clean, build clean, on Node 20.20.2. |
| **Status** | FIXED. |

## 2026-08-22 — [FINDING, P3 Night Hawk] `BREAKOUT_DYNAMIC_CAP` was deployed in production and read by nothing — the dynamic-cap kill-switch was inert under the name an operator would reach for — FIXED

> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Symptom** | Production ships `BREAKOUT_DYNAMIC_CAP = "1"` in `blackout-production/app/env`. No code path reads that name. Dynamic-N sizing was live anyway, so nothing was visibly wrong — **the deployed config matched intent by coincidence, not by the flag.** The failing operation is the inverse one: setting `BREAKOUT_DYNAMIC_CAP=0` to revert dynamic sizing changes nothing, raises no error, and gives the operator no way to tell it did not take. |
| **Root cause** | `src/lib/zerodte/breakout-cap.ts:47` read only `BREAKOUT_DYNAMIC_CAP_DISABLED`; there was no read of the bare `BREAKOUT_DYNAMIC_CAP` anywhere in `src/`. Since `resolveBreakoutCandidateCap` resolved `disabled` from that one name (line 64), an unset kill-switch meant enabled, which is the state production is in — so the inert flag was invisible from behaviour alone. Not caught earlier because **nothing compares the deploy's env keys against the names the code actually consults**; a dead key is silent in both directions. |
| **Evidence** | Found by the Night Hawk Phase 0 map's rule-8 deploy sweep (#2637, `NIGHTHAWK-MAP.md` §11 NH-2), reading non-secret flag names only from `blackout-production/app/env` via boto3. Of the twelve env-tunables that map asserts, all twelve are unset — so the code defaults are the deployed facts. Six NH-lane flags ARE set, and `BREAKOUT_DYNAMIC_CAP="1"` is one that no code reads. `grep -rn "BREAKOUT_DYNAMIC_CAP" src/` returns only the two `_DISABLED` sites. |
| **Fix** | New pure `resolveBreakoutDynamicCapDisabled(env = process.env)` honours **both** names, and `resolveBreakoutCandidateCap` now resolves at CALL time rather than from the module-eval const (so a deploy-time value is actually honoured). **Precedence is deliberate: `BREAKOUT_DYNAMIC_CAP_DISABLED` wins outright** — it is the emergency revert, and a stale `BREAKOUT_DYNAMIC_CAP=1` left in the deploy config must never be able to defeat someone actively disabling the feature mid-incident. An unrecognised value fails toward the shipped default rather than silently reverting on a typo. |
| **Blast radius** | One module, one consumer (`breakout-discovery.ts:306`). **Behaviour is unchanged for every value deployed today** — kill-switch unset + bare `"1"` resolves enabled, exactly as before, which the test suite pins explicitly. The exported `BREAKOUT_DYNAMIC_CAP_DISABLED` const is retained (unchanged, still exported) so nothing reading it breaks; it is marked deferring to the new resolver. No other NH flag in the deploy sweep was found unread. |
| **Fix rationale** | Chose to make the bare name meaningful rather than delete the deployed key: deleting it needs a production secret write, which is the riskier operation and loses the operator's evident intent. Chose kill-switch-wins over last-write-wins because the two names are not peers — one is a feature flag, the other is an emergency revert, and an emergency control that a stale flag can override is worse than no control. Deliberately did **not** make `BREAKOUT_DYNAMIC_CAP` a required enable flag: that would flip dynamic-N off for every environment that does not set it, a real behaviour change smuggled in under a config fix. |
| **Regression guard** | `src/lib/zerodte/breakout-cap.test.ts` +6 tests: neither name set → enabled (today's default); the exact deployed `"1"` → enabled (proves the no-op); `"0"/false/off/no/OFF/" 0 "` → disabled (the bug); legacy kill-switch alone; **the precedence case** (`BREAKOUT_DYNAMIC_CAP=1` + `_DISABLED=1` → disabled); and an unrecognised value not treated as a disable. Full 0DTE engine suite **1136 pass / 0 fail** on Node 20.20.2 (was 1130 before these 6); `tsc --noEmit` clean. |
| **Status** | FIXED — **pending live validation.** Merged is not done: this is a config-path change whose whole point is deploy behaviour, so it is closed only once `BREAKOUT_DYNAMIC_CAP=0` is observed to actually revert to the static floor on production, or the key is removed from the deploy. Tracked in `NIGHTHAWK-MAP.md` §11. |

## 2026-08-22 — [FINDING, P1 SPX Slayer] PB-01 and PB-02 could never fire in production: their data requirement was satisfiable only behind a gate that a decommissioned environment left permanently false — FIXED

> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Symptom** | Two of SPX Slayer's fourteen playbooks — **PB-01 "VWAP Reclaim"** and **PB-02 "VWAP Reject"**, both `fidelity: "high"` — have never matched in production. Not degraded, not blocked with a reason: absent from the matcher before any gate could record why, so nothing a member or Largo could read ever said the setups were unavailable. With `PLAYBOOK_LIVE_GATE=1` in production, a BUY requires a matched primary playbook, so every entry these two would have produced was silently not taken. |
| **Root cause** | `src/features/spx/lib/spx-desk.ts:129` gated the SPY-minute-volume VWAP proxy on `isStagingDeploy()`, which is `(NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL ?? "").includes("staging.")` (`src/lib/clerk-env.ts:10`). **Staging was fully decommissioned 2026-07-25**, so that predicate has been false in every environment that exists. The merge therefore never ran anywhere; SPX index minute bars carry no volume (ISSUE-16), so `sessionStatsFromMinuteBars` returned `vwap_volume_weighted: false` permanently; and `playbook-data-requirements.ts:73` marks `volumeWeightedVwap: id === "PB-01" \|\| id === "PB-02"`, so line 112 raised a violation on every pass, with `volumeWeightedVwapBlock` (`playbook-shadow-matcher.ts:93`) refusing the match. The chain was fully predicted in the code's own comment at `spx-desk.ts:118` — for staging's absence, which then happened everywhere. |
| **Evidence** | Production config read from `blackout-production/app/env` (named non-secret keys only): `PLAYBOOK_LIVE_GATE = "1"`, `PLAYBOOK_LIVE_ALLOWLIST = <unset>`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL = "https://blackouttrades.com"`. The unset allowlist resolves to `null`, so the allowlist was **not** the constraint — the data requirement was. Measured impact on the VWAP number itself, over 7 sessions (2026-08-12…08-21, RTH, 390 bars each) computing both VWAPs from real Polygon `I:SPX` minute bars merged with real SPY minute volume: max divergence **5.0 pts / 6.5 bps**, and the two disagree on the *side* of VWAP on **1–22 minutes per session (0.3%–5.6%)**. |
| **Fix** | Resolution extracted to `src/features/spx/lib/spx-vwap-proxy.ts` (no `server-only`, no provider import at scope — unit-testable in isolation, the same reason `spx-desk-numerics.ts` exists), gated on the new `spxVwapSpyProxyEnabled()` (`src/lib/providers/config.ts`), **default ON** so the capability ships without a secret write and `SPX_VWAP_SPY_PROXY=0` reverts it without a deploy. The day's SPY volume map is cached (60s; 15s for an empty result) because this runs on the 30s desk lane **and** inside `refreshPulseStructureCore`'s 5s cache — uncached that is ~12 full-day SPY fetches per minute per replica. Adds `vwap_volume_source: "native" \| "spy_proxy" \| null` to the desk payload. |
| **Blast radius** | The `isStagingDeploy()` dead-gate class is **~15 branches across at least nine SPX files**, not the five first recorded in `SLAYER-MAP.md` §7.1 — the undercount missed every site reaching it via `playbookStagingLabEnabled()`, which is the same predicate under another name (`playbook-session-risk.ts:47`, `trade-governor.ts:167`, `spx-play-engine.ts:875`, `spx-play-gates.ts:168,205,207`, plus `playbook-regime-router.ts:93`, `spx-play-kanban-chips.ts:131`, `SpxCommentaryRail.tsx:354`). Three more sit in `src/lib/ai-env.ts` and one in `src/lib/largo-env.ts`, outside this lane. **Only the VWAP site is fixed here**; the map now carries the corrected count and the sweep is a separate issue, because several of the rest are staging-only debug affordances whose removal is a UI change needing its own judgment. Deliberately unchanged: the `volumeWeightedVwap` requirement itself — satisfying a guard is the fix, weakening it would have shipped two playbooks on data they were specified to need. |
| **Fix rationale** | Chose to satisfy the requirement rather than relax it, and to add provenance rather than let a bare `vwap_volume_weighted: true` imply SPX volume that does not exist — the same two-metrics-wearing-one-label defect this desk already carries with max pain. Default ON rather than opt-in because opt-in would have left the playbooks dead until someone wrote a secret; env-reversible rather than hardcoded because `above_vwap` is the largest non-wall weight (±12) in the confluence engine, so this does change signals and must be revertible in seconds. Every branch fails closed **on the label**: a merge that attaches no volume reports `null`, never `spy_proxy`. |
| **Regression guard** | `src/features/spx/lib/spx-vwap-proxy.test.ts`, 16 tests: flag default/override, the three source labels, empty-map and throwing-fetch degradation, volume landing on no bar, cache hit/expiry/empty-TTL/date-rollover, and — the member-facing one — `evaluatePlaybookDataSatisfaction` for PB-01 and PB-02 blocked before and satisfied after, plus a revert-path test proving disabling the proxy re-blocks them. Full SPX lib suite 657/657 on Node 20.20.2; tsc clean. |
| **Status** | FIXED — **pending live validation**. Merged is not done: `vwap_volume_weighted`/`vwap_volume_source` must be observed true/`spy_proxy` on production, and a PB-01 or PB-02 match observed, before this is closed. |

## 2026-08-22 — [FINDING, P1 Largo] `verifyClaims` advertised 100% grounding coverage over ZERO claims — fabricated certainty in the answer payload — FIXED

> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Symptom** | A degraded Largo answer that pulled nothing — the empty-round P0 fallback — serialized `verification:{total:0,verified:0,coverage:1}`. `coverage:1` reads as "100% grounded / best possible answer" on an answer with `evidence:[]`. The number leaves the process, so any consumer that ranks or filters answers on `coverage` sees the *worst* answer as the best. |
| **Root cause** | `src/lib/bie/verifier.ts:106` — `if (claims.length === 0) return { …, coverage: 1 }`. Coverage is `verified/total`; at `total===0` that is `0/0`, and the code invented `1` as the default. The type comment said so out loud ("1 when the answer makes no numeric claims"). This is precisely the fabricated-certainty that `LARGO-PRODUCT-CONTRACT.md` forbids for `confidence`: a score a product cannot calibrate must be OMITTED, not invented, because it is compared against another lane's *measured* one. |
| **Evidence** | The raw member-path capture from the still-live empty-round P0 (coordinator, 2026-08-22 01:34Z): `HTTP 200 … "verification":{"total":0,"verified":0,"unverified":[],"coverage":1}`. Coverage 1.0 computed over zero items on a data-less answer. |
| **Fix** | `coverage: number \| null`; return `null` when `total === 0`. Null is honest ("not applicable") and forces every consumer to handle it rather than silently trusting a 1. |
| **Blast radius** | Two in-repo consumers, BOTH already gate on `total >= LARGO_GROUNDING_MIN_CLAIMS` (=4) before reading coverage — `auditLargoAnswerGrounding` (`verifier.ts:100`) and `applyVerificationCaveat` (`turn-outcome.ts:16`) — so the internal blast radius was **nil**: neither ever reached the `coverage` compare at `total===0`. The defect was purely the value that left the process. Both now also carry an explicit `coverage != null` guard so a future caller can't reintroduce the null-coerces-to-0 trap (`null < 0.5` is `true`, which would have footnoted every empty answer as low-grounding). `largo-verifier.ts:170/179` (audit log) formats null as `n/a`. tsc confirmed no other consumer of the type. |
| **Fix rationale** | Chose `null` over `0`: `0` means "0% verified" (also false — nothing was unverified either), and would trip the low-grounding footer via the same comparison. Null is the only value that says "uncalibrated" and cannot be misread as a score. |
| **Regression guard** | `src/lib/bie/bie.test.ts` — the pre-existing "no numeric claims" test updated to assert `coverage === null` (was `=== 1`); the claims-present cases (`coverage === 1` when all verified) unchanged. bie 116/116, turn-outcome 2/2 pass on Node 20; tsc clean. |
| **Status** | FIXED. |

## 2026-08-22 — [FINDING, P3 ops] The DST label check could not be satisfied by fixing a label, and never read one — FIXED

> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Symptom** | `cron-dst-audit.mjs` reported `LABEL DRIFTS` for `x-growth`, `x-replies` and `x-analytics`, with the remedy "state the UTC time and both ET renderings". That remedy had **already been applied** — `src/lib/cron-registry.ts:561-564, 575-576, 587-588` state exactly that, with comments explaining why. The verdict did not change. |
| **Root cause** | The verdict was `edt.first === est.first ? "OK" : "LABEL DRIFTS"` (`scripts/audit/cron-dst-audit.mjs:452`). For a fixed-UTC cron those two values differ by exactly one hour **by definition**, so the check was unfalsifiable — no edit to any label could ever clear it. It also never read a label: it quoted `INTENTS[key].target_et` from inside the audit and called that "the label", so the message named a stale string in the auditor rather than the deployed registry's actual text. |
| **Why it matters more than P3 suggests** | The only action that could have cleared this verdict was changing a **schedule** — and for these three routes that is outbound social cadence, not a documentation fix. A check that stays red after you do exactly what it asked, and whose only real remedy is to change unrelated production behaviour, teaches people to stop reading it. That is how a genuinely BROKEN row in the same table gets skimmed past. |
| **Fix** | An intent may now declare `utc_labelled: true`, meaning "the intent is a UTC schedule, not an ET clock". For those, the check asserts **the thing it is named for**: does the deployed label actually name UTC and both renderings? Yes → `OK (UTC-labelled)`, with the note stating both ET spans so the shift stays visible. No → `LABEL DRIFTS`, quoting the real label. |
| **What was NOT changed** | No cron schedule, in this repo or in `blackout-infra`. The hour of ET shift across the changeover is inherent to fixed-UTC scheduling and is not a defect — the question is only whether the documentation owns it, and that is decidable. |
| **Evidence** | Before: `x-growth 09:00–18:00 / 08:00–17:00 LABEL DRIFTS`, same for `x-replies` and `x-analytics`. After: all three `OK (UTC-labelled)`. **Falsifiability verified** — temporarily reverting `x-analytics`'s registry label to `"Daily 7:30 PM ET"` returns it to `LABEL DRIFTS` ("declared: Daily 7:30 PM ET"); registry restored, `git diff --stat` clean. |
| **Not fixed here — and not mine to fix** | `x-autopost` remains `BROKEN` (39 EDT fires, **0** EST). I verified it independently: UTC 12,14,16,18,20,22,0 → ET 8,10,12,14,16,18,20 under EDT, all seven inside `isPostWindow`'s weekday gate; → ET 7,9,11,13,15,17,19 under EST, **none** inside it. My lane brief forbids retuning `x-autopost`, so I have not touched it. Raised for reassignment with the analysis attached. |
| **Status** | FIXED (label check). `x-autopost` BROKEN remains OPEN and is not in this PR. |

## 2026-08-22 — [FINDING, P1 Night Hawk/Largo] `get_nighthawk_outcomes` re-truncated after #2480: the raw `pending` list was spread in AFTER the budget, re-inflating the payload past the transport cap — FIXED

> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Symptom** | `largo-truncation-probe.mjs` kept flagging `get_nighthawk_outcomes` TRUNCATED in production (last live run 2026-08-21) even though #2480 had bounded the tool's `plays` sample with `fitRowsToBudget`. The record aggregates arrived, but a tail cut still ate the end of the payload. |
| **Root cause** | The bounding in #2480 lived in `nighthawkOutcomesForLargo` (`product-reads.ts`), which fit the WHOLE record — aggregates + resolved sample — under the 14000-char budget. But the *caller*, `run-tool.ts`'s `get_nighthawk_outcomes` case, then did `const [record, pending] = await Promise.all([nighthawkOutcomesForLargo(windowDays), fetchPendingNighthawkOutcomes(7)]); return { ...record, pending };`. `fetchPendingNighthawkOutcomes` returns **full 26-column rows including the fat blob columns** (`publish_context`, `morning_verdict`, `debrief`, `grade_methodology`, `legacy_grade`). Spreading that raw list in AFTER the budget re-inflated the assembled object past `MAX_TOOL_RESULT_CHARS` (16000), and `anthropicToolLoop`'s tail slice cut it — the exact class #2480 fixed for `plays`, reintroduced through a second list the budget never saw. |
| **Evidence** | Live probe re-run 2026-08-22 (pre-deploy) was **INDETERMINATE, not a reproduction** — the ongoing tool-dispatch P0 meant `get_nighthawk_outcomes` was never called (`"called": false`; Largo returned the empty-answer fallback), so the control could not be proven and the run self-reported UNVERIFIED per the harness's own rule. The truncation mechanism is instead confirmed **statically in code** (the raw-spread-after-budget path above), which is stronger and P0-independent. Note also the probe's own control IS `get_nighthawk_outcomes` at 180d — the same tool — so the live probe is a weak instrument for this specific finding regardless of the P0. New unit test measures the mechanism directly: 30 fat pending rows (~15KB each) spread raw = **> 16000 chars** (asserted, non-vacuous guard), while the assembled result stays **≤ 16000**. |
| **Fix** | Move pending's fetch AND its budgeting into `product-reads.ts` so **one authority** bounds the whole result. New pure `assembleNighthawkOutcomesForModel({aggregates, resolvedRows, pendingRows})` leans every row (`leanNighthawkOutcomeForModel` drops the five blob columns the model never used), budgets `plays` then `pending` with `fitRowsToBudget` measured over the WHOLE object, and emits `pending` LAST so a residual tail cut eats the pending sample before the record. `nighthawkOutcomesForLargo` now fetches pending in parallel and delegates. `run-tool.ts` simplifies to `return nighthawkOutcomesForLargo(windowDays);` — the raw spread is gone. Fixed at the SOURCE (aggregate/limit inside the tool), NOT by raising `MAX_TOOL_RESULT_CHARS`. |
| **Fix rationale** | Pending is dropped to the same lean projection as resolved because the blob columns are per-ticker forensics the model never consumes from this tool — a ticker's full context is `get_nighthawk_dossier`. `NIGHTHAWK_PENDING_MAX_SAMPLE = 20` is a reading ceiling; `fitRowsToBudget` is the real bound. `NIGHTHAWK_PENDING_LOOKBACK_DAYS = 7` preserves the prior run-tool value verbatim. The assembler is pure so a test proves the size bound without a database (the fetches are DB-backed and unreachable from the sandbox). |
| **Blast radius** | `get_nighthawk_outcomes` was the only caller that spread a raw secondary list after the budget — swept the other Night Hawk tools in `run-tool.ts`; the rest return a single already-budgeted product read. `fetchNighthawkOutcomeAnalytics` is still imported/used at run-tool.ts:1785 (a different tool); only the now-unused `fetchPendingNighthawkOutcomes` import was removed. |
| **Regression guard** | `src/lib/largo/product-reads.test.ts` — new describe block: (a) `leanNighthawkOutcomeForModel` drops all five blob columns + `id`; (b) the WHOLE assembled result (74 fat resolved + 30 fat pending) stays ≤ `MAX_TOOL_RESULT_CHARS`, with a guard asserting raw pending alone exceeds the cap so the test cannot pass vacuously; `decided_count` and `pending_total` survive, pending sample is leaned. 32/32 in file pass on Node 20. |
| **Status** | FIXED. |

## 2026-08-22 — [FINDING, P2 Vector/Largo] `opexContext` anchored "today" to the UTC date, dropping OpEx Friday's own expiry every evening — FIXED

> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Symptom** | Asked "when is the next OpEx?" on an OpEx Friday **evening** (after 20:00 ET), Largo's `get_vector_analytics` OpEx block answered next month's expiry instead of "today". The same question at 14:00 the same day answered correctly — the failure was time-of-day dependent, which is why it survived. |
| **Root cause** | `opexContext` (`src/lib/largo/vector-analytics-core.ts:297`) computed the reference "today" as `new Date(nowMs).toISOString().slice(0, 10)` — the **UTC** calendar date. Between 20:00 ET (00:00 UTC) and midnight ET the UTC date has already rolled to tomorrow while the ET trading day is still today. On OpEx Friday that made `today` = Saturday, so the same-day OpEx got `days_away = -1`, was dropped by the `days_away >= 0` filter, and `next` jumped a full month. This is the *exact* off-by-one the block's own instant→day comment was written to prevent — reintroduced through the timezone, one layer down. |
| **Evidence** | At `nowMs = 2026-08-22T00:30:00Z` (20:30 ET Fri 08-21, a real OpEx Friday): OLD `today = 2026-08-22` → `days_away(08-21) = -1` (dropped, `next` = 2026-09-18); NEW `today = 2026-08-21` → `days_away(08-21) = 0` (`next` = today). Measured both paths directly. |
| **Fix** | Anchor to the shared ET session date: `etSessionDate(nowMs) ?? new Date(nowMs).toISOString().slice(0, 10)`. `etSessionDate` was **already imported** in this file (line 49) and used for the structure/event ET anchors — this call site simply had not adopted the centralized helper. A non-finite `nowMs` yields `null`, in which case the fallback preserves the prior behaviour rather than fabricating a date. |
| **Fix rationale** | Only the QUERY WINDOW moves; which Fridays are OpEx remains entirely `opexDatesInRange`/`thirdFriday`'s call (those correctly compute date-only values in UTC — a bare date has no timezone, so their UTC anchoring is not the same defect). No alternative (e.g. a market-calendar dependency) is warranted for a window-start date. |
| **Blast radius** | Swept the Vector surface for the same class (`toISOString().slice(0,10)` / `getUTC*` used as a business date). `vector-forecast-target.ts:91` (`nextYmd`) operates on a date-only string and is correctly UTC-anchored — not a defect. `vector-daily-regime-server.ts:78` (`todayYmd`) has the same UTC skew but only in the ET-evening window when the market is closed and the session already settled; weekend/closed sessions return nothing regardless, so no member-visible wrong number results — noted as lower-severity, not fixed in this PR to keep it surgical. |
| **Regression guard** | `src/lib/largo/vector-analytics-core.test.ts` — new test "OpEx Friday EVENING still reads as today" asserts `next.date == 2026-08-21` and `days_away == 0` at the ET-evening boundary. Verified non-vacuous: the old UTC-slice logic produces `days_away = -1` for that input (shown above). Full file 16/16, C1 ratchet 6/6, analytics-wiring 17/17 pass on Node 20. |
| **Status** | FIXED. |

## 2026-08-22 — [FINDING, P1 cost/ops] The AI-spend ceiling that silently disabled Largo was invisible to every operator surface — FIXED

> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Symptom** | On 2026-08-21 the org-wide daily Anthropic ceiling tripped and Largo began answering *"I couldn't pull enough live data to answer that"* to every question. Nothing showed the ceiling was close, nothing showed it had tripped, and nothing showed it afterwards. Establishing the cause took a full day and three refuted hypotheses (a BIE ingestion PR, the ceiling, then the ceiling again). |
| **What was NOT broken** | `ai-spend-ledger.ts` maintains an exact cross-replica daily total and `anthropic.ts` consults it before every model call. Both worked correctly. The kill switch did precisely what it was built to do. |
| **Root cause** | **No operator surface ever read the ledger.** "How close are we to the ceiling?" could only be answered by shelling into Redis — and raw TCP to Redis is blocked from the audit sandbox entirely, so from here it could not be answered at all. A guardrail whose state is unobservable cannot be managed; it can only be discovered by the outage it causes. |
| **My own contribution to the outage** | I fanned four lanes onto simultaneous live Largo probes against a metered service without checking the meter, on top of another lane's ~15 probe calls and my own truncation probe. Those probes both helped trip the ceiling and biased the sample to nothing-but-failures. That is a control-plane error, not a lane error. |
| **Fix** | `src/lib/ai-spend-headroom.ts` grades spend against the armed ceiling — `ok` / `warning` (≥75%) / `tripped` / `disabled` / `unknown` — and `admin-health` now reads the ledger, exposes `ai_spend` on the payload, and raises the verdict through the same synthetic-issue machinery as a saturated Postgres pool. A `tripped` ceiling gates `health_ok`, because Largo refusing member queries is not a healthy system however green everything else looks. |
| **The distinction that decides the design** | **`disabled` is never reported as `ok`.** The kill switch is opt-in, so an unarmed ceiling and abundant headroom are different facts, and collapsing them is how a guardrail stays unarmed forever — the console reads green either way. Likewise an unreadable ledger is `unknown`, never `ok`: a spend figure that failed to load is exactly when a runaway loop is least visible. Both raise a warning issue rather than staying silent. |
| **Warning reports dollars, not just a percentage** | *"$20.00 left before Largo stops answering"* is actionable at 3am; *"80% of ceiling"* requires the reader to remember the ceiling and do arithmetic. |
| **Blast radius** | `admin-health` is the console's single health read (`use-admin-data.ts`), so the field and the issue appear wherever health already renders. The Redis read is defensive — any failure degrades to `unknown` and surfaces as such rather than dropping the field. Counts and `health_ok` were hand-maintained per synthetic issue and are updated in the same style, so the issue list and the counts cannot disagree. |
| **Regression guard** | `src/lib/ai-spend-headroom.test.ts` (8 tests): ok raises nothing, the warn boundary is inclusive and configurable, at/over ceiling is critical, **every falsy ceiling shape is `disabled` and explicitly asserted not-`ok`**, every unreadable-spend shape is `unknown`, zero spend is `ok` not `unknown`, and the tripped message names the member-visible consequence. |
| **Deliberately NOT done** | No ceiling value changed, no probing behaviour changed, and no alerting added beyond the existing issue channel. Per-lane spend attribution — which lane spent what — is a separate and larger piece of work; this answers only the org-wide question that caused the outage. |
| **Status** | FIXED. |

## 2026-08-22 — [FINDING, P1 Largo] An empty tool-loop round produced a member-facing wrong answer and left no trace of its cause — FIXED (visibility)

> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Symptom** | For most of 2026-08-21 into 08-22, Largo answered *"I couldn't pull enough live data to answer that"* to questions whose data was demonstrably present. Raw capture, 01:34Z: **HTTP 200**, `tools_used: ["live_feed_capture"]` (prefetch only, no answering tool), `evidence: []`. In the same minute `GET /api/market/gex-positioning?ticker=SPY` returned `available:true, spot 766.27, gamma_posture "short", net_vex +$332B` — fresh. Naming the tool explicitly (*"Use get_positioning to…"*) declined too, as did the decline message's own suggested fallback. |
| **Where it originates** | `anthropicToolLoop`, the no-tool-calls branch: a round returning neither `tool_use` blocks nor text returns `null`, and the caller renders that null as the data-excuse fallback. The advice is not merely unhelpful, it names the wrong cause — a member is told to try a different question when the question was fine. |
| **The real defect recorded here** | Not the empty round itself — that may well be upstream model behaviour and legitimately nothing to fix. The defect is that **nothing distinguished the two possibilities**: (a) the model returned no `tool_use` block at all, or (b) the model asked for a tool and we dropped it. (a) is upstream and closes the matter; (b) is ours and is severe. |
| **Why it stayed unknown for a day** | `persistClaudeTurn` (`turn-outcome.ts:73`) writes only the FINAL answer, `tools_used` and captured results — no per-round record. So the stored turn shows exactly what an external capture already shows and nothing more. **Three independent harnesses across three lanes each reproduced the symptom and not one could tell (a) from (b).** Three causes were proposed and each refuted by measurement: a BIE ingestion PR (refuted — it was not in the deployed image), the daily AI-spend ceiling (refuted — the route returns an honest 503 and this returned 200), and the ceiling again the following night (same refutation). |
| **Fix** | The empty-round branch now logs the round's shape — round index, model, block count and block-type list — plus the member-visible string it produces, at the one point where the distinction still exists. `"round 0 … blocks=0[]"` is a model that returned nothing; a non-empty block list with no `tool_use` is a different story entirely. |
| **Fix rationale — why so narrow** | The log fires ONLY when the round has no tool calls **and** no text. A tool-less round WITH text is the normal way a turn ends; logging those would bury the one line that matters under every healthy turn, and a signal nobody can find is the same as no signal. That narrowness is asserted by the guard, so widening it later cannot silently destroy the thing it was added for. |
| **Deliberately NOT done** | No behaviour change. The loop returns exactly what it returned before. This does not fix the P0 — it makes the P0 diagnosable, which is the actual blocker. Persisting per-round state to the turn row (so the question is answerable after the fact, not only from live ECS logs) is the larger follow-up and is NOT in this change. |
| **Regression guard** | `src/lib/providers/anthropic-empty-round-visibility.test.ts` (5 tests), a source assertion for the same reason as `anthropic-stream-guard.test.ts`: inducing an empty round needs the real API, since the client is acquired via `getClient()` and is not injected. Verified non-vacuous — deleting the log fails exactly 3 of the 5, and restoring it passes all 5. |
| **Status** | FIXED (visibility only — the empty round itself is OPEN and may prove to be upstream). |

## 2026-08-22 — [FINDING, P1 ops] Merges stopped reaching production for ~5 hours and nothing noticed — merging is loud, deploying is silent — FIXED (detection)

> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Symptom** | Three commits touching `src/**` and `public/**` sat on `main` from 00:36Z to ~04:38Z with **no `ecr-push-production` run**. Nothing was red. CI, CodeQL and Deploy-smoke all fired on the same pushes; the deploy workflow alone did not. The concrete member-facing symptom was `https://blackouttrades.com/images/diagrams/what-is-gex.svg` returning **404** — an asset merged hours earlier that had never shipped. |
| **How it was found** | By the SEO lane trying to verify its own PR on production, not by any coordinator check. I ran the release loop through the entire window and never asked whether merges were reaching prod. My own cycle instructions say to confirm the deploy after a merge wave; I only ever checked when I cared about one specific fix. |
| **Root cause of the blindness** | **Merging is loud and deploying is silent.** A merge posts a green check and a notification. A deploy that never *starts* posts nothing at all — there is no run to be red, no event to subscribe to, no artifact to inspect. The absence has no signal, so "merged" gets read as "shipped". (The trigger-side cause of the stall itself is NOT diagnosed here; GitHub delivered the push events — 13 CI runs on `event=push` in the same window — and only this one workflow failed to create runs.) |
| **Why a naive check would be useless** | `ecr-push-production.yml` has a `paths:` filter, so "no deploy since the last merge" is USUALLY correct and healthy — a docs or audit-script merge is not supposed to deploy. A check that ignores the filter cries wolf on every docs merge and gets switched off within a day. |
| **Fix (detection, not cause)** | `scripts/audit/deploy-freshness.mjs` + pure core `scripts/audit/lib/deploy-freshness-eval.mjs`. It asks the narrow answerable question: **is there a commit matching the deploy paths with no deploy run created after it?** Uses run *creation*, not completion — a queued run proves the push was seen, which is what is being checked. Missing input is `unknown`, never `ok`. |
| **The check found its own cry-wolf on run 1** | It flagged `fe642703` — a commit whose only deploy-path file was `src/meridian-invariants.test.ts`. That legitimately matches the workflow filter but **cannot change what a member is served**. Reporting it as "production is behind" is true of the workflow and false of production. Severity is now SPLIT (`member-facing` vs `test-only`) rather than suppressed, because a deploy workflow that does not fire is a real fault at any severity. |
| **Evidence** | The three stalled commits carried 2, 6 and 4 deploy-path files respectively, so the path filter does not explain them. Replayed as a fixture: the check returns `behind` with exactly those three and correctly excludes the audit-script commit in the same window. |
| **Regression guard** | `src/deploy-freshness-eval.test.ts` (11 tests): path matching incl. a sibling-directory prefix trap, docs-only is OK, the real incident is `behind`, a queued run clears a commit, missing input is `unknown`, no-runs-at-all is `behind` not `unknown`, an unparseable date is skipped, and the test-only severity split both ways. |
| **Deliberately NOT done** | The stall's own cause is unfixed and unexplained. This makes it **visible in minutes instead of hours**; it does not prevent it. Wiring the check into a schedule, and root-causing why GitHub created no run for a matching push, are both open. |
| **Status** | FIXED (detection only — the underlying trigger fault is OPEN). |

## 2026-08-22 — [FINDING, P1 Meridian] The banner rebuilt the cross-event comparison #2614 had just removed — it paired the UPCOMING print's implied with LAST quarter's reaction under an "Expected vs realized" label — FIXED

> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **How it was found** | Running the #2614 live validation owed on #2615. The sweep passed — `evr_compares_across_events` **7 → 0**, all six rules at zero on 10/10 events — so I ran a control to check the rule had not simply stopped firing because the field vanished. It had not: the payload was correct. The **component** was not. A payload-level check cannot see a comparison that is reassembled in JSX. |
| **Symptom, measured on prod 2026-08-22 06:2xZ (build `f09f0609`, which contains #2614)** | **PDD** renders: label *"Expected vs realized"* · headline *"Last print realized **−2.35%**"* · sub *"Implied ~**9.2%** into print"*. The −2.35% is the **2026-05-27** print. The 9.2% is implied into the **2026-08-24** print. Three months apart, under a comparison label, with *"into print"* attaching the implied to the same print as the realized. **GFI is sharper still** — its last print is **2026-03-30**, ~5 months before the 16.5% implied for Aug 25. |
| **Scope** | **7 of 10** high-impact earnings events in the cohort render it (PDD, BNS, BMO, HEI, GFI, ZM, INTU). The other three (XPEV, DKS, SMTC) are hidden only because #2613's expiry gate leaves them with no forward implied, so the headline is null — they are hidden by accident, not by design. |
| **Root cause** | #2614 withheld the `ratio` and the `verdict` but still **passed the forward implied through** as `expected_vs_realized.expected_move_pct`, and `MeridianEarningsTabs.tsx:184` sourced its sub-line from `pack.expected_move_pct` — the upcoming print's implied — independently of the block entirely. Suppressing the computed comparison did not suppress the rendered one. **A number a consumer must not pair does not belong in the block.** |
| **Fix** | Three layers, so no single one has to hold. (1) `buildExpectedVsRealized` checks cross-event **first** and returns `expected_move_pct: null` — the forward implied is dropped, not passed through. (2) A new **`same_event: boolean`** on the type states outright whether the two numbers are commensurable, so any consumer — including Largo — can tell without re-deriving it from `print_history`. (3) The banner reads its label and sub-line from that flag and from the block, never from the pack: cross-event renders as **"Last print reaction"** with no sub-line. |
| **A no-op removed** | With both call sites now passing only the per-print implied, `patchMeridianEnrichmentExpectedMove` recomputed byte-identical inputs and was provably dead — `enrichment` is built fresh by `loadMeridianEarningsEnrichment` in the same request, not read from a cache, so it had nothing stale to upgrade. It is deleted along with `meridian-earnings-event-load-core.ts`. It was also the last place the pack's forward move touched this block, guarded by a condition unrelated to what it did — a ready-made argument for reintroducing the coupling. |
| **A second, live defect fixed in the same block** | `meridian-earnings-enrich.ts` passed `session_change_pct` as the realized side while the patch path used `reaction_pct`. That is the BMO/AMC anchoring trap: **INTU's last print reads −1.67% by session and −20.02% by reaction**. The enrichment value is *served* whenever the patch early-returned for want of a chain-IV move — i.e. exactly the XPEV/DKS/SMTC rows. Both paths now use `reaction_pct ?? session_change_pct`. |
| **A deliberate behaviour widening, called out** | Cross-event with **no** implied on either side previously returned `headline: null` (the missing-implied guard ran first), so XPEV/DKS/SMTC displayed nothing despite holding a settled, sourced reaction. They now publish *"Last print realized −1.56%"*. The reaction does not need an implied to be true. This makes a banner appear where none appeared before — flagged here so a reviewer can disagree with it specifically. |
| **Deliberately NOT changed** | `MeridianImpliedVsRealized` (History panel) also takes the forward implied, and it is **correct**: it compares that one number against the **distribution** of the last n reactions (`n = 8 prints · absolute moves`) — the standard implied-vs-realized read, and a legitimate use of a forward quote. The defect is pairing it with **one specific prior print**. Left alone. |
| **Blast radius** | The expected-vs-realized block and its one banner. `realized_move_pct` is unchanged. No level, gate, score, ranking or price moves. The type gains a required field, so every producer is forced by `tsc` to state which case it is in. |
| **Live regression guard** | Two new rules in `scripts/audit/lib/meridian-invariants.mjs`, so the production sweep catches this class rather than only its first instance: **`evr_carries_foreign_implied`** (a block flagged `same_event: false` must not carry an implied at all) and **`evr_claims_without_same_event`** (a ratio or verdict on a block that admits it is cross-event). Both fire only on an **explicit** `same_event: false` — an absent flag is an older payload, not a claim, and a checker that lights up through every deploy window stops being read. |
| **Regression guard** | `meridian-evr-same-event.test.ts` rewritten (+7): the implied is dropped on cross-event and kept on same-event; `same_event` is set on every branch; the reaction publishes with no implied; no reaction means no headline; the enrich call site passes `priorImplied` alone (`priorImplied ?? expectedMovePct` asserted **absent**); the realized side is asserted to be the reaction; the deleted patch is asserted gone; and the banner block is asserted to contain **no** `pack.expected_move_pct` in its `sub=`. `meridian-invariants.test.ts` +4. |
| **Gates on Node 20.20.2** | `npx tsc --noEmit` clean · `npm test` **10032 pass / 0 fail / 1 skipped** · `npm run build` clean · `npx eslint` clean. |
| **Status** | FIXED — this PR. Live proof owed: re-read PDD and GFI on the deployed build and confirm the label reads "Last print reaction" with no implied sub-line, and that the sweep reports zero `evr_carries_foreign_implied`. |
