## 2026-08-06 — [P0, real-money-adjacent] 0DTE→Day-Trade discovery-ceiling widening (dte≤1→dte≤4) + mandatory Swing dual-admission fix
> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Severity** | P0 — structural discovery starvation (the "why fewer plays" question from the entry above, now resolved with live evidence) plus a genuine cross-engine dual-admission bug caught by adversarial review before ship. |
| **Trigger** | Member: "just 3 plays over the entire day for 0dte... if we have the code correctly setup we will have 10 plays for mag7 itself on a single trading day... look at GOOGL, PLTR, ANET — so many stocks moved on 0dte but our system does not catch one of the plays." Requested a full ground-up 0DTE redesign; reframed "0DTE" mid-discussion to mean **Day Trade** — a position opened and closed within the session, using whatever the nearest LISTED expiry is, not a contract that must itself expire same-day. |
| **Root cause** | Every 0DTE discovery admission gate (`board.ts`'s `SETUP_MAX_DTE`, `breakout-source.ts`'s `pickAtmZeroDteContract`/`pickBreakoutContractWithFallback`, `pin-source.ts`'s `pickAtmPinContract`, `scan-trigger.ts`'s `EVENT_MAX_DTE`) was hardcoded to `dte≤1`. But the **majority of single-name equities list NO Mon–Thu weekly expiry at all** — only Friday. So on any day other than Thursday/Friday, `dte≤1` structurally excludes almost every single name from the board, regardless of how strong its move was — the board was never "bad at catching" GOOGL/PLTR/ANET, it was mathematically unable to reach their nearest listed contract on a Monday–Wednesday. Live CloudWatch evidence (`/ecs/blackout-production-market-worker`, a live Wednesday scan tick) confirmed this directly: **88 of 99 BREAKOUT candidates rejected as `no_same_day`** in one tick. The grading math itself was NEVER the constraint — `gates.ts`'s G-15-removal note had already proven in production that the same-day session-clock EXIT discipline (15:30 close, ratchet exit) holds correctly for dte=1; nothing about it is specific to dte=0 or dte=1 versus dte=2–4. |
| **Why dte≤4, not unlimited** | `ZERODTE_MAX_DTE=4` is a sanity backstop, not a target width: worst case (Monday → that week's Friday expiry) is exactly 4 calendar days. The nearest-expiry-first sort in every contract picker means widening the ceiling only RELAXES the admission bar — it can never cause a farther contract to be preferred over a nearer one that already exists. |
| **Adversarial-review-caught bug (would have shipped a real dual-admission defect)** | A 3-proposal design→judge→synthesize workflow, followed by 3 independent adversarial reviews of the synthesized design, unanimously caught that the synthesized design's own claim ("widening `HORIZONS.SWING.dteMin` alone preserves non-overlapping windows") was **false**. `horizons.ts` is read for UI display only (`serving-board.ts`) — it is NEVER consulted by Swing's actual commit-time admission gate. That gate is `src/lib/swing/taxonomy.ts`'s `SWING_SUB_LANES.TACTICAL.dteMin` (read directly by `gates.ts`'s `expiry_insufficient` check) and `src/lib/swing/event-trigger.ts`'s `SWING_EVENT_MIN_DTE` — two SEPARATE hardcoded constants that do not derive from `horizons.ts` at all. Had the 0DTE ceiling widened to dte≤4 without these two constants moving in lockstep, a dte 2–4 contract would have been **simultaneously admissible to BOTH the 0DTE board (`deriveContractHorizon` → `ONE_DTE`) and Swing's TACTICAL sub-lane (`subLaneForDte`)** — the same signal double-committed as two unrelated plays, each independently sized and risked. Caught and fixed before any code shipped, not discovered live. |
| **Second bug caught (fallback toggle would have silently become a no-op)** | The initial widening draft for `breakout-source.ts`'s `pickBreakoutContractWithFallback` collapsed the two-phase 0DTE→1DTE fallback into a single unconditional `maxDte=ZERODTE_MAX_DTE` call, which would have made the live operator toggle `ZERODTE_BREAKOUT_ALLOW_1DTE=0` (strict-0DTE-only mode) silently inert. Caught by 2 of 3 adversarial reviewers; fixed by keeping the two-phase structure (`maxDte = breakoutAllow1DteFallback() ? ZERODTE_MAX_DTE : 0`) so the toggle still forces strict-0DTE-only exactly as before. |
| **Third gap caught (real-time reaction-speed regression for the exact new target population)** | `scan-trigger.ts`'s `EVENT_MAX_DTE=1` — the real-time event trigger that wakes the board within ~45s of a big swept print — was not part of the original design scope. Left unwidened, the newly-admissible dte 2–4 population (Friday-only-weekly names on a Mon–Wed) would have reacted only on the next ~5-minute cron tick instead of the fast path, degrading exactly the population this fix targets. Widened in lockstep. |
| **Fix (Phase 1 — this PR)** | `horizons.ts`: new exported `ZERODTE_MAX_DTE=4` as the single cross-engine ceiling; `HORIZONS.ZERO_DTE.dteMax` and `HORIZONS.SWING.dteMin` now derive from it (`[0,4]`/`[5,30]`, was `[0,1]`/`[2,30]`). `board.ts`: `SETUP_MAX_DTE` re-exported from `ZERODTE_MAX_DTE` (same name, so call sites need no edit); `deriveContractHorizon` now admits `dte∈[1,SETUP_MAX_DTE]` as `ONE_DTE` (was `dte===1` only). `breakout-source.ts`: `pickAtmZeroDteContract`'s default `maxDte` now `ZERODTE_MAX_DTE`; `pickBreakoutContractWithFallback` widened via the fallback-preserving ternary (see above). `breakout-discovery.ts`: the (pre-existing, dead-code) miss-reason diagnostic's dte literal updated to match. `pin-source.ts`: `pickAtmPinContract`'s default `maxDte` now `ZERODTE_MAX_DTE`. `scan-trigger.ts`: `EVENT_MAX_DTE` now sourced from `ZERODTE_MAX_DTE`. **Mandatory Swing-side fix (same PR, per adversarial review):** `swing/taxonomy.ts`'s `SWING_SUB_LANES.TACTICAL.dteMin` now reads `HORIZONS.SWING.dteMin` directly (was hardcoded `2`) instead of a second, independent copy; `swing/event-trigger.ts`'s `SWING_EVENT_MIN_DTE` likewise now reads `HORIZONS.SWING.dteMin` (was hardcoded `2`). `swing/gates.ts`: one stale comment string updated (its logic already read `spec.dteMin` dynamically, so no behavior change was needed there). `strategy-version.ts`: `DISCOVERY_VERSION` v4→v5, `CONTRACT_SELECTOR_VERSION` v1→v2 — partitions pre/post-widening `ONE_DTE` rows into separate calibration cohorts via the existing `strategy_config_hash` mechanism (design Q12) so this remains evidence-honest. New `dual-lane-overlap.test.ts`: sweeps every dte in [0,90] asserting the 0DTE board and Swing's sub-lanes never both admit the same dte — the direct regression test for the bug the adversarial review caught. `flow-persist.ts` deliberately left UNCHANGED — its `dte≤1` discounted-premium-floor rationale (0DTE-specific extrinsic-value decay) does not hold for dte 2–4, so widening it would have been unsound; confirmed against the review's own finding. |
| **Deliberately NOT changed / deferred (Phase 2–4, evidence-gated)** | `PLAN_RULES` stop/target levels, `CHASE_PCT` entry-chase scaling, `GOVERNOR_ENFORCE_PREMIUM_BUDGET`, `GOVERNOR_MAX_SESSION_STOPS` — all stay byte-identical across the whole dte 0–4 window until real dte-bucketed backtest evidence (via `zerodte-sim.mjs --grade`, bucketed by `actual_dte_at_commit`) says a recalibration is warranted, per the repo's calibration-first law. PIN-universe expansion (adding names like PLTR/ANET to the scanned set) and the "0DTE"→"Day Trade" UI copy rename are separate, smaller follow-up PRs — this PR is scoped to the discovery-ceiling fix and its mandatory Swing-side correction only. Iron Condor's cash-settled-index-only restriction (`condor.ts`) is an explicit, intentional safety gate (unmodeled early-assignment risk on American names) — untouched by this widening. |
| **Evidence (tests)** | `horizons.test.ts`: 9/9 pass. `board.test.ts`: 109/109 pass (2 tests updated for the dte 0-4/5+ boundary, 1 new dte-4/dte-5 flow-tape case added). `taxonomy.test.ts`: 6/6 pass (boundary tests updated for the [5,30] Swing window). `event-trigger.test.ts`: 6/6 pass (dte 4/5 boundary cases added). `gates.test.ts`: 16/16 pass (unaffected — its dynamic `spec.dteMin` read required no logic change). `breakout-source.test.ts`: 16/16 pass (dte 2/4/5/7 boundary cases added to both the raw picker and fallback-wrapper tests). `breakout-discovery.test.ts`: 11/11 pass (no changes needed — walk-until-built behavior unaffected). `scan-trigger.test.ts`: 6/6 pass (dte 2-4/5 boundary cases added). `pin-source.test.ts`: 9/9 pass (dte 2/4/5 boundary cases added). `strategy-version.test.ts`: 11/11 pass (no literal-version assertions existed to update). `dual-lane-overlap.test.ts` (new): 2/2 pass — the direct cross-engine regression proof. |
| **Blast radius** | New: `dual-lane-overlap.test.ts`. Modified: `horizons.ts` + `.test.ts`, `board.ts` + `.test.ts`, `breakout-source.ts` + `.test.ts`, `breakout-discovery.ts`, `pin-source.ts` + `.test.ts`, `scan-trigger.ts` + `.test.ts`, `swing/taxonomy.ts` + `.test.ts`, `swing/event-trigger.ts` + `.test.ts`, `swing/gates.ts` (comment only), `strategy-version.ts`, `docs/audit/0DTE-DESIGN-DECISIONS.md` (Q2 marked resolved). Explicitly verified NOT to need changes: `flow-persist.ts` (dte≤1 discount floor stays scoped to genuine 0DTE only), `swing/gates.ts`'s actual gating logic (already dynamic), `pin-discovery.ts` (calls `pickAtmPinContract` with no explicit `maxDte`, so it picks up the new default automatically). |
| **Fix rationale** | Sourced the ceiling from ONE file (`horizons.ts`) with every consumer importing it, rather than bumping five independent hardcoded `1`s to `4`s in place — this is the direct structural fix for the exact failure class that caused this bug (independent copies of the same boundary silently drifting apart). Chose the fallback-preserving ternary over collapsing `breakout-source.ts`'s two-phase pick, specifically to avoid silently disabling a live operator toggle. Chose to widen `scan-trigger.ts` in lockstep rather than leaving it for a later PR, since shipping the wider discovery ceiling without the matching fast-path would have left the exact target population (Mon–Wed weekly-only names) reacting slower than the population already covered. Used a multi-agent design→judge→synthesize→adversarial-review workflow (rather than a single linear design pass) specifically because the stakes warranted it — the adversarial review step demonstrably earned its cost, independently catching a real, severe, would-have-shipped bug (Swing dual-admission) that both the original synthesized design AND a manual second read had missed. |
| **Status** | FIXED — shipped and verified present in `main` on 2026-08-08 by `scripts/audit/findings-verify-stale.mjs` (found: `SETUP_MAX_DTE`, `pickAtmZeroDteContract`, `pickBreakoutContractWithFallback`). Restamped from a mid-flight status that was never revisited. |

## 2026-08-06 — [P3, tooling, audit harness auth] Temp Clerk user creation aborted the whole run on a PHONE-number collision (only e-mail collisions had a recovery path) — FIXED (fix/audit-temp-user-phone-collision)
> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Severity** | P3 — tooling/availability, not data correctness. No product, member-facing, trading-logic or grading behaviour is involved. It matters because the standing **13:32 UTC weekday market-open validation trigger** (`docs/audit/MARKET-OPEN-VALIDATION.md`) runs UNATTENDED: a recoverable identifier clash was surfacing as a hard RED on the validation gate. |
| **Session** | Live audit pass, 2026-08-06 17:33 UTC (market open). `scripts/audit/data-validator.mjs` failed at the very first step; an immediate bare re-run succeeded. |
| **Symptom** | `[FAIL] auth: create/adopt temp user — {"errors":[{"message":"This phone number is already associated with an existing account..."}]}` / `TOTALS {"FAIL":1}` — the run exits non-zero having validated NOTHING. |
| **Root cause** | `scripts/audit/data-validator.mjs:266-273` (pre-fix) and the ~20 copy-paste clones of the same block. Clerk enforces uniqueness on BOTH identifiers the harnesses hand it — the e-mail AND the phone — but the recovery path assumed the collision was always the e-mail: it matched the shared `form_identifier_exists` code on the whole payload and then looked the existing user up **by e-mail** (`GET /users?email_address=…`) to adopt it. When the clash is on the PHONE, that lookup returns nothing, `userId` stays null, and the run dies with no retry — even though simply drawing a different number would have worked. Two things make the clash actually happen: (a) `lib/audit-phone.mjs` `generateDefaultAuditPhone()` draws from `+1415555{0000..9999}` = 10,000 values, and with ~30 audit temp users alive at once on a busy day that is a ~4.5% birthday-collision chance per run; (b) every leaked temp user (a run whose end-of-run DELETE didn't stick) holds its number **forever**, permanently burning that value. **Why it wasn't caught earlier:** task #175 fixed the *previous* incarnation of this bug (a single hardcoded `+14155550123` default that got permanently burned) by randomizing the suffix — which converted a deterministic 100%-failure into a low-probability one, and the recovery path's e-mail-only assumption was never revisited. Two nearby scripts also used *narrower or non-random* draws that made a clash likelier still: `exhaustive-platform-audit.mjs` used `Date.now() % 9000` (deterministic per millisecond — two harnesses started together drew the SAME number) and `rth-browser-test.mjs` drew from only 900 values. |
| **Evidence** | The live failure above, verbatim, plus the fact that an identical immediate re-run passed — the run's inputs were fine, only the random phone draw was unlucky. The e-mail-vs-phone discrimination is now pinned by a unit test built on that EXACT payload (`{"message":"This phone number is already associated with an existing account."}`), which carries **no `meta.param_name`** — so the discriminator needs the human-readable message fallback and cannot rely on the structured param alone. Pre-fix, `isClerkEmailCollision` on that payload was effectively "true" (the old check regexed `form_identifier_exists` across the whole payload) and it took the dead e-mail-lookup branch. |
| **Fix** | One implementation of create-or-adopt in `scripts/audit/lib/clerk-audit-user.mjs`, used by every harness: `classifyClerkCreateFailure` splits the two collisions (structured `meta.param_name`/`meta.paramName` first, message regex as belt-and-braces); an **e-mail** collision still adopts the leftover user and re-PATCHes its metadata (unchanged behaviour); a **phone** collision REDRAWS a fresh `+1415555XXXX` and retries, bounded at 5 attempts, then fails with a message that names the exhaustion. Anything else (bad key, rate limit) fails fast on attempt 1 — retrying can't fix it. A caller-pinned `AUDIT_PHONE` is honoured on attempt 0 only; retries always redraw, so an operator override that is itself taken can't pin the loop. Transport-agnostic core + two adapters (`createOrAdoptAuditUserViaCurl` for the spawnSync-curl family, `createAuditClerkUser` for the fetch family) so no harness keeps its own copy. |
| **Blast radius** | The bug had ~20 copies. Converted to the shared helper in this PR — `scripts/audit/`: `data-validator.mjs`, `zerodte-e2e-healthcheck.mjs`, `zerodte-e2e-suite.mjs`, `swing-e2e-healthcheck.mjs`, `firewall-rth-replay.mjs`, `gex-wall-snapshot-poll.mjs`, `veto-flicker-capture.mjs`, `vector-bead-probe.mjs`, `zerodte-sim-feed.mjs`, `nighthawk-prod-check.mjs`, `nighthawk-deploy-verify.mjs`, `force-nighthawk-rebuild.mjs`, `seo-visibility-audit.mjs`, `screenshot-0dte.mjs`, `rth-browser-test.mjs`, `tier-access-e2e.mjs`, `nav-first-click-repro.mjs`, `deep-security-audit.mjs`, `deep-security-audit-phase2.mjs`, `premium-security-audit.mjs`, `lib/vector-audit-auth.mjs`, `lib/admin-e2e-auth.mjs`, `lib/keyless-clerk-session.mjs`; `scripts/`: `comprehensive-endpoint-audit.mjs`, `exhaustive-platform-audit.mjs`, `rth-comprehensive-sweep.mjs`, `vector-e2e-audit.mjs`, `prod-admin-login-smoke.mjs`, `validate-admin-users-e2e.mjs`, `validate-clerk-config.mjs`, `validate-prod-ux-cto.mjs`, `validate-prod-ui-full.mjs`, `validate-prod-signin-redirect.mjs`, `x-live-autopost.mjs`, `x-showcase-post.mjs`. Already routed through the shared helper and fixed for free: `lib/prod-clerk-session.mjs`, `lib/ios-playwright-auth.mjs`, `grid-zerodte-e2e-audit.mjs`, `spx-dashboard-e2e-audit.mjs`. `grep -rn form_identifier_exists scripts/` now returns hits ONLY inside the shared helper. |
| **Known residual** | `validate-admin-users-e2e.mjs` also creates users through the APP's own admin route (`{ body: { phone: generateDefaultAuditPhone() } }`, 3 sites) — that path asserts a 201 from the product route and is deliberately left as-is: adding a retry there would mask a genuine route failure, which is what the E2E is for. |
| **Tests** | `scripts/audit/lib/clerk-audit-user.test.mjs` rewritten, 14 tests, `npx tsx --test` → 14/14. Covers: the exact live payload classifying as phone-not-e-mail; camelCase `meta.paramName`; N phone failures then success with a FRESH number each attempt (asserts every retry draws a distinct value AND that attempt 0 honoured the caller's number); a pinned `AUDIT_PHONE` that is taken not being re-sent on retry; exhaustion after `maxPhoneAttempts` with a phone-collision message; the e-mail-collision adopt path still adopting + re-PATCHing and NOT spinning the phone loop; both identifiers colliding at once → adopt; a non-collision error failing fast on attempt 1; async transports; and both curl adapters end-to-end against a fake curl (asserting a phone clash never triggers the e-mail lookup). |
| **Verification** | `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. All `scripts/audit/lib/*.test.mjs` → 64/64. `node --check` on all 36 edited `.mjs` files. `verify-api-auth-guards` GREEN (189 routes) + tailwind-apply guard clean. Repo `src/**/*.test.ts` suite: 6270/6280 — the 10 failures are pre-existing and cannot be caused by this diff (`git diff origin/main --name-only | grep -c '^src/'` → 0). GitHub Actions was in a `major_outage` at PR time, so verification was local; the PR was NOT auto-merged. |
| **Status** | FIXED on `fix/audit-temp-user-phone-collision` → PR to `main`. NOT auto-merged (Actions outage — merge once CI's `verify` gate can run and is green). |

## 2026-08-06 — [P0, ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED + FIXED] `updateSwingLiveState` has ALWAYS thrown Postgres 42P08 — the swing live-state UPDATE never parsed, so `last_mark`/peak/trough were never written for ANY swing position (members saw "CURRENT +$0.00" on live-money positions)
> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Severity** | **P0** (upgraded from the initial P2 read once the root cause was pinned). Not a two-row anomaly: the statement is universally unparseable, so NO swing position has ever had a live mark latched. Members watching live-money positions were shown a precise, confident, WRONG `+$0.00` instead of an honest "unknown", and every premium-based rung (profit ladder, `premium_stop` −60% backstop) is permanently inert for want of a mark. Capital-preservation stops still worked throughout — the manager reads the FRESH quote (`manage-sync.ts:279 lastMark: numOrNull(reads.mark)`), never `row.last_mark`. |
| **Live evidence** | `GET /api/market/nighthawk/horizons?view=swings` (organic — NOT Legacy-origin) shows two OPEN swing positions committed 2026-08-06T10:00:34Z: **SPCX** SHORT (put, strike 120, exp 2026-08-21) and **MSFT** LONG (call, strike 480, exp 2026-08-14). Both show `livePnlPct: null, peakPremium: null, troughPremium: null` at 14:37 UTC (~4.5h / multiple 15-min active-refresh cron ticks after commit, well into RTH), and STILL null across 3 more polls at 14:46/14:48/14:49 UTC. Directly cross-checked MSFT's exact held contract against Polygon live (`GET /v3/snapshot?ticker.any_of=O:MSFT260814C00480000`): **200 OK, real live NBBO** (bid 19.50 / ask 21.45 / last 19.87, OI 1024, fresh `last_updated`) — so the upstream data is unambiguously available; the gap is somewhere in the app's own mark-fetch/write path (`swing-active-refresh` route's `loadOptionMark` → `occSymbolFromSwingRow` fail-closed-on-`contract_occ` → `fetchOptionsUnifiedSnapshot` → `updateSwingLiveState`'s `last_mark = COALESCE($3, last_mark)`), not a Polygon/data availability problem. |
| **Root cause (CONFIRMED 2026-08-06, amends the original "unconfirmed" entry above)** | `updateSwingLiveState` (`src/lib/db.ts:6591-6626`) **never executed — not once, for any swing position.** node-pg issues queries over the EXTENDED protocol with UNTYPED parameters, so Postgres assigns each param its type at its FIRST **coercion** site. `$3` (mark) survives by accident: its first occurrence is `last_mark = COALESCE($3, last_mark)` (db.ts:6617), which types it `numeric`. `$4` (`underlyingMfe`) and `$5` (`underlyingMae`) had NO earlier occurrence — their first appearance was the bare NullTest `CASE WHEN $4 IS NOT NULL ...` (db.ts:6620-6621). A NullTest coerces nothing, so parse analysis aborted with **SQLSTATE 42P08 `could not determine data type of parameter $4`**. The later `COALESCE(underlying_mfe, $4)` inside the same CASE arm does NOT rescue it (verified empirically, not inferred from the grammar). Because the whole statement fails to PARSE, the correctly-typed `$3` columns never land either — which is why `last_mark`/`peak_premium`/`trough_premium` stayed NULL. **This is a latent first-exposure defect, not a regression:** every prior cron tick in the retained log window logged `positions=0`, so the statement had never been exercised against a real open row until today's 10:00:34Z commit. |
| **Why members saw `+$0.00` (second, independent defect)** | With `last_mark` NULL, `live-plays.ts:53` served `mid: mark ?? entry` — laundering "unknown" into "exactly flat". `adapters.ts:482 fin(src.contract.mid)` put that on `TerminalPlay.mark`, `terminal-display.ts:345 markDollarPnl` computed `mark - entry = 0`, and the hero rendered `+$0.00`. **The renderer was never at fault** — `TerminalPremiumPanels.tsx:147-152` already falls back to `—` when the dollar P&L and pct are both null. The read path fabricated the number before the renderer ever saw it. |
| **Evidence (direct reproduction, not inference)** | (1) **Local PG16 repro:** stood up PostgreSQL 16.13, created `swing_positions` from the DDL extracted PROGRAMMATICALLY from db.ts (no transcription) and ran the UPDATE text extracted programmatically from db.ts through node-pg's extended protocol with the production tuple `[id, status, mark, mfe, mae]`. All three tuples — `[1,'OPEN',20.1,496.62,496.62]`, `[1,'HOLD',14.825,null,null]`, `[1,'OPEN',null,null,null]` — THREW `42P08 could not determine data type of parameter $4`; the row after all three attempts still read `last_mark=null, peak_premium=null, trough_premium=null` — byte-for-byte the production symptom. (2) **Fix verified in the same harness:** with `$4::numeric`/`$5::numeric` all four ticks succeed AND every documented semantic holds — peak ratchets UP only (20.1 held when the mark fell to 18), trough ratchets DOWN only, a null mark is a silent no-op, and the status ladder still refuses `HOLD → PENDING`. (3) **Prod counter signature reconciled:** `/ecs/blackout-production` logged `positions=2 refreshed=0 snapshots=2 skipped=0 errored=2` on ~19 consecutive 15-min ticks from 10:20:36Z to 15:45:48Z. `active-refresh.ts:98-101` increments `snapshotsAppended` when `snapshotId != null` and `errored` when `outcome.error` is set, and `manage-sync.ts:486-487` runs `insertSnapshot` then `updateLiveState` in ONE try — so `snapshots=2` AND `errored=2` pins the throw strictly to `updateLiveState`. The 11:00 tick's `refreshed=1 closed=1` is NOT a counter-example: the roll/close path returns at `manage-sync.ts:456-463` WITHOUT ever calling `updateLiveState`. (4) **Member impact through the app:** `horizons?view=swings` served SPCX `entryPremium 16.68 / contract.mid 16.68` and MSFT `entryPremium 14.4 / contract.mid 14.4`, both `livePnlPct/peakPremium/troughPremium` null — mid falling back EXACTLY to entry is the proof `last_mark` is NULL (raw PG TCP is blocked here). Live Polygon NBBO at the same moment: `O:MSFT260814C00480000` mark 19.5–20.1, i.e. **~+36% unrealized that the member could not see**. |
| **Blast radius (established by EXECUTION, not pattern-matching)** | **Swing lane only.** `updateZeroDteLiveState` (db.ts:6165, `zerodte_setup_log`) and `updateBangerLiveState` (`banger/positions-db.ts:181`) use the same `GREATEST/LEAST` NullTest idiom but are SAFE — each types its param one line earlier via `last_mark = COALESCE($n, last_mark)`. Both were executed verbatim against a matching local table: OK, rowCount 1, latches correct. `updateSwingLiveState` is the **only** writer of `swing_positions.last_mark`/`peak_premium`/`trough_premium` in the repo (its sole call site is `swing-active-refresh/route.ts:209`), so the whole swing lane's premium latch was dark. Note: the comment at db.ts:1691-1692 claiming "two writers (cron sync + live-marks lane)" is stale — there is one. |
| **Why CI missed it** | `src/lib/db-swing-ledger.test.ts:320/336-360/442` assert on the SQL **source string** with regexes (`assert.match(body, /WHEN status IN .../)`) and never execute the statement against a Postgres. **A statement that cannot be parsed still matches its own text**, so it passed every existing guard. |
| **Fix** | Three independent changes, ascending blast radius: **(1) READ PATH** — `src/lib/swing/live-plays.ts:53` `mid: mark ?? entry` → `mid: mark`. `ChainContract.mid` is already `number \| null`, so this is a value change, not a contract change; with mid null the EXISTING renderer fallback shows `—`. `livePnlPct` was already correctly null and is untouched. **(2) OBSERVABILITY** — `swing-active-refresh/route.ts` now `console.error`s the per-position `outcome.error` (id + ticker) that `manage-sync.ts:495` captured and `active-refresh.ts:98` then discarded. That discard is what kept a 100%-failing real-money write invisible for 5.5h of RTH. **(3) WRITE PATH (root cause)** — `src/lib/db.ts:6620-6621` `WHEN $4 IS NOT NULL` → `WHEN $4::numeric IS NOT NULL` (same for `$5`), with a WHY comment stating the rule: **a param's FIRST occurrence must be a coercion site or carry an explicit cast, never a bare `IS [NOT] NULL`.** Nothing else changed — same columns, same monotonic ratchets, same status CASE. |
| **Deliberately NOT changed** | The status CASE ladder, the GREATEST/LEAST ratchet semantics, `occSymbolFromSwingRow`'s fail-closed OCC policy, and `loadOptionMark`'s best-effort null. The suspected secondary defect (null `contract_occ` → null mark → `COALESCE` preserves NULL) is NOT in play: `fetchOptionsUnifiedSnapshot` was run against prod's own provider and returned a live mark for BOTH held OCCs. The fail-closed OCC guard was deliberately left alone rather than pre-emptively loosened. |
| **Why safe to ship during RTH** | The manager does not read the columns this UPDATE writes — `manage-sync.ts:279` passes `lastMark: numOrNull(reads.mark)`, the FRESH quote — so the per-tick verdict is identical before and after. `peak_premium` is read only at `scale-out.ts:181` inside the `scaledAlready === true` branch (dead input while false). The four rungs that can close/roll (`roll.ts:128` GATING_RUNGS) run off `reads`, not the row. The single coupling is status → TRIM → `scaledAlready`, and TRIM can only latch when the profit ladder fires TAKE_PARTIAL at mark ≥ 2.0× entry — neither open position is near that, so status can only move OPEN → HOLD today. Known cost: peak/trough/MFE/MAE seed from the CURRENT mid-session mark rather than the true session peak, so today's two rows carry a truncated excursion window into the multi-truth grader — strictly better than all-NULL, but not a clean session. |
| **Tests (both FAIL without the fix — verified by reverting)** | `src/lib/db-swing-ledger.test.ts`: (a) a **Postgres-backed EXECUTION test** that builds `swing_positions` from db.ts's own DDL, extracts db.ts's own UPDATE text, and runs it through node-pg's extended protocol with the production tuple, asserting the marks land AND that the ratchets/status ladder are unchanged — reverting the cast reproduces `code: '42P08'`. It reads `SWING_TEST_DATABASE_URL` and SKIPS (never fails) when absent; `ci.yml` now runs a `postgres:16` service container so the gate is real in CI. A psql literal or an in-memory PG fake would NOT reproduce this — neither performs real extended-protocol param type inference. (b) a **structural invariant** test scanning every SQL template in db.ts for a param whose first occurrence is an untyped `IS [NOT] NULL`. NOTE: the first draft of that scanner passed on the BROKEN source — it counted db.ts's own prose mention of `$4` inside a SQL `--` comment as a coercion site. It now strips SQL comments and ignores NullTests quoted inside them, and asserts a minimum match count so it can't rot into a no-op. A purely static check here is exactly the trap that let this bug ship. `src/lib/swing/live-plays.test.ts`: a null `last_mark` must serve `contract.mid === null` (not entry), and a real mark must still pass through. |
| **Post-deploy verification** | On the first tick after deploy expect `refreshed=2 errored=0` in `/ecs/blackout-production` and non-null `livePnlPct`/`peakPremium` on `GET /api/market/nighthawk/horizons?view=swings`. If `errored` is still non-zero, the new per-position `console.error` now carries the actual pg message. |
| **Status** | FIXED — shipped and verified present in `main` on 2026-08-08 by direct inspection (`src/lib/swing/live-plays.ts:133` reads `mid: mark`, not the pre-fix `mid: mark ?? entry`). Restamped from a mid-flight status that was never revisited. |

## 2026-08-10 — [P1, capability] Largo's per-question tool allowlist hid a mean 81% of the platform from the model, and its own safety fallback was unreachable dead code — FIXED (fix/largo-full-tool-surface)
> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Severity** | **P1, capability (not correctness-of-numbers).** No number Largo printed was wrong — the accuracy rails held. The defect is that for a large class of plainly on-topic questions Largo could not reach the tool that answers them, and answered anyway from the live feed alone. A confident answer built on a partial read is the failure mode the system prompt's "no invented data" rule exists to prevent, arrived at from the other direction: the model wasn't hallucinating, it was never shown the door. |
| **Root cause** | `getToolsForIntent()` (`src/lib/largo/tool-defs.ts:1034` pre-fix) ran the question through ~20 hand-written regexes (`intent-keywords.ts`) and returned an ALLOWLIST. `largo-terminal.ts:273` then did `LARGO_TOOL_DEFS.filter(t => allowed.has(t.name))`, so tools that missed the regexes were not de-prioritised — they were **absent from the request**. The model had no way to know they existed. |
| **Evidence (measured, not asserted)** | Ran 20 realistic member questions through the real `getToolsForIntent`. Mean exposure **21.9 / 116 tools (19%)**. Worst cases, all at the 4-tool floor: `"what's the biggest risk in my open positions"` (cannot reach `get_open_plays`), `"how many trades did we win last month"` (cannot reach `get_trade_history` / `get_zerodte_record`), `"what did the desk get wrong yesterday"`, `"anything worth trading into the close"`, `"give me your best idea"`. Best case `"walk me through the whole platform right now"` reached 86/116. |
| **Second defect — the fallback never ran** | The guard `if (names.size <= 2) { ...CORE_TOOLS }` was **unreachable**. The seed set unconditionally added 4 names (`get_market_context`, `get_platform_snapshot`, `get_ecosystem_context`, `get_hot_tickers`), so `names.size` was never ≤ 2. Brute-forced 1,444 two-word phrasings: the minimum is exactly 4, every time. `CORE_TOOLS` has never executed in production. Two tests in `tool-defs.test.ts` cited that branch in their doc comments as the thing they were protecting against. |
| **Third defect — the gate defeated its own purpose** | The gate exists to save tokens. It does the opposite. `anthropic.ts:497` places `cache_control:{type:"ephemeral"}` on the LAST TOOL, making the tool block the first prompt-cache prefix. A per-question list changes that prefix on nearly every turn, so it **never cached**: ~5,176 tokens at full price for a typical ticker question. The full static surface is 17,025 tokens written once and billed at the cache-read rate on every subsequent turn. Static-and-complete wins on capability and, past the first turn of a session, on cost. |
| **Why it wasn't caught** | The failure is silent by construction — a missing tool produces a plausible answer, not an error. And the tests encoded the bug's own worldview: every one asserted "phrasing X reaches tool Y", which passes trivially whenever the regex happens to match, and says nothing about the phrasings nobody thought to write down. `intent-keywords.ts`'s doc comments are a record of that chase — several describe a specific member phrasing that reached the wrong tool set and the pattern added to catch it. |
| **Fix** | `largo-terminal.ts` passes `LARGO_TOOL_DEFS` verbatim — full surface, every turn. `getToolsForIntent`, `mentionsTicker` and `CORE_TOOLS` deleted, replaced by a comment recording both traps so neither is rebuilt. |
| **Blast radius / deliberately unchanged** | `intent-keywords.ts` is NOT dead and was left alone: `question-intent.ts` still uses it to pick which LIVE FEED blocks to prefetch, and `largo-followups.ts` uses `NIGHTHAWK_RE`. That is a different job — choosing what data to warm is a cost/latency call where a miss degrades an answer; choosing what tools to expose was a capability call where a miss made an answer impossible. The 12-round loop cap, 4096 max tokens, per-user and org concurrency gates, daily budget and AI-spend kill switch are all untouched, so the cost ceiling is unchanged. |
| **Tests** | `tool-defs.test.ts` 54/54. The per-phrasing allowlist tests are replaced by one strictly stronger invariant — the surface is complete and uniform — which asserts on the specific tools whose absence caused the silent failures above and fails loudly if per-question filtering returns. |
| **Known limits of this verification** | Unit-level only. `largo-terminal.test.ts` (7 tests) does not run in this sandbox — `mock.module is not a function` on Node v22.22.2 — and fails identically on `main`, so it is a pre-existing runner gap, not a regression. The behavioural claim (better answers to the questions listed above) is **not yet proven against prod**; Largo is admin-gated, and the live A/B is the next step. |
| **Status** | Code FIXED and merged. Live validation OPEN. |

## 2026-08-10 — [P2, dead architecture] Largo's BIE answer-ROUTER was already bypassed but still compiled in, and its retrieval layer had been returning `[]` in production since it shipped — REMOVED (fix/largo-drop-bie-router)
> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Context** | Owner direction: *"It should not be using any BIE… Largo should become the universal intelligence layer across BLACKOUT, not a generic chatbot and not dependent on BIE… Do not hard-code question types."* This entry records what "BIE" actually turned out to BE inside Largo, because the name covers four unrelated things and only two of them were the problem. |
| **What was actually dead** | `src/lib/largo/bie-route.ts` exported `tryBieRoute`, which classified a question into one of ~20 fixed intents and composed a canned answer. **Nothing called it.** `finalizeBieRoutedTurn` and `BieTurnResult` in `turn-outcome.ts` existed solely to service it and were likewise unreferenced. Largo has been answering every turn through the Claude tool loop already — `largo-terminal.test.ts`'s own case is literally named *"every turn uses the Claude tool loop (no BIE router)"*. So the router was compiled, type-checked and maintained while being unreachable. |
| **What was dark** | `largo-terminal.ts` called `searchKnowledge()` on **every turn** and spliced hits into the system prompt. `searchKnowledge` returns `[]` unless `bieEmbeddingsConfigured()`, i.e. unless `VOYAGE_API_KEY` is set — and that variable appears nowhere in `blackout-infra`. Every Largo turn since this shipped paid a call + try/catch to receive an empty array. The retrieval layer was never grounding anything. |
| **What was NOT the problem (deliberately kept)** | "BIE" also names (a) the data readers Largo's tools call — `ecosystem-context`, `internal-api`, `provider-read`, `vector-full-state`, `hot-tickers`, `wall-dynamics-read`, `cortex-read`, `full-platform-loader`, `largo-live-prefetch`; (b) the answer ENVELOPE the UI renders as evidence/level/scenario cards; and (c) the claim VERIFIER (`collectContextNumbers`/`verifyClaims`) that traces every figure in an answer back to data pulled that turn. Deleting these would remove Largo's access to the platform and its anti-fabrication guard — the exact opposite of the instruction they arrived with. They are being RELOCATED into `@/lib/largo/`, not removed. |
| **Fix** | Deleted `bie-route.ts`, `finalizeBieRoutedTurn`, `BieTurnResult`. Dropped `classifyBieIntent`/`bieFollowups` from `largo-followups.ts` — that short-circuit returned an intent's canned chip list, making suggestions a function of which hard-coded bucket a phrasing landed in, which is precisely the "custom route per phrasing" shape the rebuild removes. Dropped the `searchKnowledge` block. Inlined `bieIntentBucket(null)`, whose whole body was `intent ?? "claude_fallback"`, as a named constant so historical rows still bucket identically in `bie/calibration.ts`. |
| **Member-facing side effect** | The low-coverage caveat footer said *"BIE verification: N of M figures…"*. Renamed to *"Data check:"* — a member-facing string should never have carried an internal subsystem's name. `turn-outcome.test.ts` asserted on the literal `/BIE verification/`; it now asserts the caveat states the count and the reason, and additionally asserts the text contains no `BIE` at all, so the branding can't creep back. |
| **Orphaned by this change (not yet deleted)** | `bie/router.ts`, `bie/composers.ts`, `bie/decompose.ts` and `bie/dynamic-format.ts` now have **zero** non-test consumers outside `src/lib/bie/` itself. Left in place in this PR to keep the blast radius to Largo; they are a clean follow-up deletion. `bie/knowledge.ts` still has two real consumers (`admin/bie-report`, `cron/db-cleanup`) so it stays. |
| **Verification limits** | `largo-terminal.test.ts` does not run in this sandbox (`mock.module is not a function`, Node v22.22.2) and fails identically on `main` — it is a pre-existing runner gap, and it is also the suite that covers the turn path most directly, so CI is the real gate for this change, not the local run. |
| **Status** | Code REMOVED. Module relocation and the orphan deletion OPEN as follow-ups. |

## 2026-08-10 — [P2, silent-wrong-data] `GET /api/market/nighthawk/horizons?view=<unknown>` returned the 0DTE lane with HTTP 200 instead of a 400 — a caller could not tell "that view does not exist" from "that lane is empty" — FIXED (fix/horizons-silent-view-fallback)
> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **How it was found** | `scripts/audit/largo-truth-divergence.mjs`, a new probe that reads the SAME field from every surface that claims to know it and reports disagreement. It flagged `nighthawk/horizons` as ABSENT for a graded-win-count read; chasing that turned up the real defect underneath. |
| **Live evidence (measured 2026-08-10, prod, admin session)** | Identical byte counts prove the fallback: `?view=swings` → **34,352 bytes**; `?view=` (empty) → **34,499 bytes** (full payload); and `?view=outcomes`, `?view=totally-invalid-view`, `?view=zerodte` → **1,053 bytes each, byte-identical** — the 0DTE lane. All five returned HTTP **200**. |
| **Root cause** | `parseNightHawkView` (`src/features/nighthawk/lib/nighthawk-view.ts:80`) returns `DEFAULT_NIGHTHAWK_VIEW` for any unrecognised string. That is CORRECT for the UI — a stale shared link should still render a board rather than a blank error page. The route (`horizons/route.ts:39-40`) then did `viewParam ? horizonForView(parseNightHawkView(viewParam)) : null`, so a truthy-but-unknown param narrowed the payload to the DEFAULT lane. A forgiving parser is right; using it as an API validator is not. |
| **Why it matters more now than before** | Largo reaches internal routes through `call_internal_api`. With the full 116-tool surface it composes URLs itself, so it can invent a plausible view name — `outcomes` is exactly the kind of guess an LLM makes — receive the 0DTE lane with a 200, and report it fluently. That answer would be **grounded** (every number traces to the response it was handed) and **contract-conforming**, and still wrong. No answer-side validation can catch a wrong-lane 200; only the API refusing can. |
| **Fix** | New `isKnownNightHawkView` + `KNOWN_NIGHTHAWK_VIEW_TOKENS` (one source of truth for the parser's aliases and the validator, so an alias cannot be added to one and missed by the other). The route now 400s on an unrecognised non-empty `view`/`horizon`, returning the allowed list. `parseNightHawkView` is deliberately UNCHANGED — the fix is at the API boundary, and a test pins the forgiving default so a future edit does not "helpfully" harden it and blank stale shared links. |
| **Blast radius** | Route-local. `?view=` empty and every valid alias behave exactly as before; only previously-silent bad input changes, from a misleading 200 to an explicit 400. |
| **Tests** | `nighthawk-view.test.ts` 17/17, including: every known token accepted case-insensitively; the exact production strings (`outcomes`, `totally-invalid-view`, `record`, `0dtee`) rejected; a bidirectional drift check (every token parses to a real view AND every view is reachable by some token); and the forgiving parser default preserved. |
| **Status** | FIXED. |

## 2026-08-10 — [P4, cosmetic API asymmetry] `/api/market/quote?ticker=I:SPX` 400s while `?ticker=SPX` works — NOT a Largo defect
> **kind:** `NEGATIVE-RESULT`

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **What was seen** | The truth-divergence probe logged `UNREACHABLE quote(I:SPX) HTTP 400 {"error":"Invalid ticker"}` for both SPX and VIX. |
| **Why it is NOT a bug worth chasing** | The route's allowlist `/^[A-Z0-9.\-]{1,8}$/` (`quote/route.ts:182`) deliberately excludes `:` — the comment states it validates before any paid upstream call to avoid wasting a Massive snapshot and inflating cache/telemetry cardinality. `?ticker=SPX` returns the correct index price (`7757.64`, matching Polygon exactly), and `/api/market/indices` is the index surface. **Largo is unaffected**: `get_quote` → `toolQuote` (`run-tool.ts:261-276`) has its own `I:` branch calling `fetchIndexSnapshots`, and never touches this HTTP route. |
| **Recorded because** | The `get_quote` tool schema advertises `"e.g. NVDA, SPY, SPX, I:SPX"`, so the next person who sees a 400 on `I:SPX` will reasonably suspect the tool. It is a different code path. Left unchanged rather than widening a deliberately tight validator for a case with no consumer. |
| **Status** | NO ACTION — documented so it is not re-investigated. |

## 2026-08-11 — [P1, product-blocking] Largo REFUSED to generate a card ("I cannot generate images"), on the screen that renders the card generator — FIXED (fix/largo-image-refusal, #2050)
> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **How it was found** | The operator asked Largo, in the live terminal, "Can you generate me an image for todays Night Hawk plays" and screenshotted the reply. |
| **Live evidence** | Verdict: *"I cannot generate images. I'm a market data analysis tool — I read live feeds, options flow, dealer positioning, and trade records. Image generation is outside my scope."* Bottom line: *"…if you want to build a visual yourself, I'll give you the raw numbers … you can paste them into a chart tool or screenshot the [Night Hawk] page directly."* Rendered directly ABOVE the working card generator's `AUTO / X LANDSCAPE / PNG` controls and a correctly-rendered card of the five plays it had just listed in prose. |
| **Root cause** | `src/lib/largo/system-prompt.ts` describes six desks, 121 tools and fourteen rich component types, and never mentions that a turn can be rendered as a PNG. The model was not reasoning badly — it refused a capability it had no way to know existed. Same class as the extractor defects in this series (*a real capability with no path to the layer that needs it*); here the missing path was KNOWLEDGE, not data. |
| **Fix** | A prompt section stating the card exists, that its controls are on screen, and that it is composed from the answer AND this turn's tool results — so the completeness of the answer IS the completeness of the graphic. Also states what Largo must not do: describe layout, offer to "design" anything, or invent a URL. The empty-turn case stays honest — no tool output means the answer is the missing data under **Data**, not a refusal. |
| **Tests** | `system-prompt.test.ts` 10/10 (+2), asserting both the capability claim and the provenance rule, so a future trim fails CI instead of silently restoring the refusal. |
| **Status** | FIXED — merged 2026-08-11. |

## 2026-08-11 — [P2, self-contradicting output] The card packer's block heights had NEVER been compared to pixels: "no room on this card" printed above 23% blank canvas — FIXED (fix/largo-card-packer-heights, #2051)
> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **How it was found** | Rendering a live card and looking at it, then reproducing it offline with a new harness, `scripts/audit/largo-card-deadspace.mjs`. |
| **Live evidence** | A composed portrait card printing `ALSO MEASURED, NO ROOM ON THIS CARD: DEALER LEVELS · FLOW · GAMMA PROFILE · METRICS` above **314px of blank canvas (23.3%)**. Landscape: 152px (24.1%). Both statements cannot be true. |
| **Root cause** | `composeCard` packs against per-block height ESTIMATES and none had ever been checked against what satori draws. Measured, one block per render: `verdict` 354 est / **259** drawn (it assumed 26 chars per line at 70px, but `Headline` steps its font DOWN as text lengthens, so a long headline draws more chars per line and shorter lines — both errors the same way); `playbook` 290 / **146** (a row is padding 9×2 + a 20px line + a 6px gap ≈ 48px, priced at 128); `flow_tape` 302 / **375** — wrong in the DANGEROUS direction, a block packed at a size that would run into the pinned footer and its mandatory disclaimer. The packer also charged nothing for the ~20px section margin between blocks. |
| **Why it was never caught** | The estimates are internally consistent and the whole suite passed. Nothing in the repo could see pixels. |
| **Fix** | `verdictHeight()` mirrors `Headline`'s own step-down over the real content width and stops pricing a summary on dense surfaces where the template drops it; `playbook`/`flow_tape`/`levels`/`regime` constants set from measurement; new `blockGap(spec)` charged per block after the first. |
| **Measured result** | Dead canvas 314px → **89px** (23.3% → 6.6%) portrait, 152px → **55px** landscape; every block's estimate/drawn ratio moves from 0.50–1.38 to **0.96–1.26**; the dealer-level map now appears instead of being reported as truncated. |
| **Tests** | +2 (estimate within 0.85–1.35 of measured drawn height, naming the calibration command in the failure message; `used` must equal block sum PLUS gaps). Two existing tests changed because they had locked in a CONSEQUENCE of the mis-estimation — one was protecting an overflow, the other asserted a de-dup outcome rather than its invariant. 237/237. |
| **Status** | FIXED — merged 2026-08-11. |

## 2026-08-11 — [P3, shareable-artefact defect] Card headlines ended `….` — three copies of one truncator, two of them wrong — FIXED (fix/largo-truncation-ellipsis, #2052)
> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Live evidence** | An NVDA card headline ending *"…a $225 call wall holding resistance**….**"* — four dots. |
| **Root cause** | `headlineFromMarkdown` sliced at 89 chars, `trimEnd()`ed, and appended an ellipsis onto whatever character the slice landed on — here the sentence's own full stop. **Blast radius:** three copies of the same function existed and disagreed — `answer-format.ts` (no word-boundary back-off AND no punctuation strip — the one that shipped the artefact), `x-content-humanize.ts` (word boundary, no punctuation strip — same defect latent on the X autopost path), and `generic-extract.ts` (correct, written when this class of bug was found on card labels; the fix never travelled). |
| **Fix** | The correct copy promoted to `src/lib/truncate-text.ts` and used by all three. Both properties are load-bearing: back up to a word boundary (only when the break lands in the final third, so an unbroken OCC symbol or URL is still cut rather than collapsing the string), and strip trailing punctuation before the ellipsis. |
| **Tests** | `truncate-text.test.ts` 5/5, including the exact live shape asserted against `/[.,;:\s–—-]…$/` and word-boundary integrity checked by `startsWith` against the source. |
| **Status** | FIXED. |

## 2026-08-11 — [P3, relevance] A card generated for "how does NVDA look today" drew a playbook of NET, NVDA and CRM — FIXED (fix/largo-card-subject-relevance, #2053)
> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Root cause** | Composition ranks BLOCKS against the question (`scoreBlock`) and then each block draws its ROWS in whatever order the engine published (`pb.rows.slice(0, cap)`). Relevance is applied at one level and ignored at the level the member reads, so a question naming one instrument gets the whole edition's top of book. |
| **Fix** | `subjectFirst(rows, subject, cap)` — a stable partition promoting the subject's rows, applied to the playbook block. CONDITIONAL by design: rank carries meaning, so promotion happens only when the subject's row would otherwise be CUT OFF by the cap. If it is already drawn, the published order stands. |
| **Tests** | 3 — promotion suppressed when already visible and applied when not; stable partition asserted on `rank` values so a re-rank cannot pass; every no-op case. |
| **Status** | FIXED. |

> **kind:** `FINDING`

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Symptom** | NVDA options-play answers: headline badge said BULLISH while verdict said mixed/bearish; put wall cited at flow strike (212.5 vs dealer 190); EMA stack inverted; same thesis printed 3–4 times (system reads + signal table + comparison block); centered Anton headline read like a widget not a desk answer. |

(3) `assessEditionActionability` always set `existingThesis: true`. (4) Renderer printed every envelope field without dedupe. (5) Mobile native terminal never passed `question` → trade layout always default. |
